title.zh: 卷五十四 列傳第四: 王世充 竇建德
title.en: Volume 54 Biographies 4: Wang Shicong, Dou Jiande
title.raw: 卷五十四 列傳第四: 王世充 竇建德 Volume 54 Biographies 4: Wang Shicong, Dou Jiande

sentences.zh: 王世充，字行滿，本姓支，西域胡人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, styled Xingman, was originally surnamed Zhi; he was a Hu man from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, whose courtesy name was Xingman, was originally of the surname Zhi—a man of Hu origin from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 寓居新豐。

translations.literal: He lived as a resident in Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His family had settled in Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 祖支頹耨，早死。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi Tuinou died early.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi Tuinou had died young.

sentences.zh: 父收，隨母嫁霸城王氏，因冒姓焉，仕至汴州長史。

translations.literal: His father Shou, following his mother in remarriage to the Wang family of Bacheng, therefore took their surname; he rose to serve as chief administrator of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shou had gone with his mother into a remarriage with the Wang clan of Bacheng and taken their surname; he eventually served as chief administrator of Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世充頗涉經史，尤好兵法及龜策、推步之術。

translations.literal: Shichong was broadly versed in the classics and histories, and especially fond of military methods and the arts of tortoise divination and calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had read widely in the classics and histories and was especially devoted to military science, tortoise-shell divination, and calendrical reckoning.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，以軍功拜儀同，累轉兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era, through military merit he was appointed Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, and was repeatedly transferred until he became an assistant in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang reign he won appointment as Bearer of the Imperial Insignia for military service and was promoted step by step to assistant in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 善敷奏，明習法律，然舞弄文法，高下其心。

translations.literal: He was skilled at memorial writing and well versed in law, yet he manipulated legal texts and bent them to his own inclinations.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote memorials fluently and knew the law well, yet he twisted legal texts to suit his own purposes.

sentences.zh: 或有駁難之者，世充利口飾非，辭議鋒起，眾雖知其不可而莫能屈。

translations.literal: When anyone rebutted him, Shichong with a sharp tongue glossed over wrongdoing and raised a storm of argument; though all knew he was in the wrong, none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone challenged him, Shichong answered with a glib tongue, papered over his errors, and flooded the debate with words; everyone knew he was wrong, yet no one could best him in argument.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累遷江都丞，兼領江都宮監。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was repeatedly promoted to assistant prefect of Jiangdu and concurrently overseer of the Jiangdu palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he rose repeatedly to assistant prefect of Jiangdu and concurrently overseer of the Jiangdu palace.

sentences.zh: 時煬帝數幸江都，世充善候人主顏色，阿諛順旨，每入言事，帝必稱善。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor made many visits to Jiangdu; Shichong was adept at reading the sovereign's expression, flattering and agreeing with his wishes; whenever he entered to speak on affairs, the Emperor always praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited Jiangdu often; Shichong watched his mood closely, flattered him, and agreed with whatever he wished. Each time he came forward with business, the Emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 乃雕飾池臺，陰奏遠方珍物，以媚於帝，由是益暱之。

translations.literal: He then ornamented pools and terraces and secretly memorialized on rare goods from distant lands to please the Emperor, and thereby grew even closer to him.
translations.idiomatic: He had pools and terraces lavishly decorated, secretly reported exotic tribute from distant regions, and so drew the Emperor even closer.

sentences.zh: 世充知隋政將亂，陰結豪俊，多收群心，有繫獄抵罪，皆枉法出之，以樹私恩。

translations.literal: Shichong knew Sui government was about to fall into disorder; he secretly allied with bold men, gathered many hearts, and whenever anyone was imprisoned for a crime he released them by bending the law, thereby building private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Sui rule was collapsing, he quietly cultivated bold men, won people over, and whenever someone sat in prison he bent the law to set them free and bind them to himself in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感作亂，吳人朱燮、晉陵人管崇起兵江南以應之，自稱將軍，擁眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling raised troops in the Jiangnan region in response, styled themselves generals, and mustered more than a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling answered him with armies in the south, styled themselves generals, and gathered more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 隋遣將軍吐萬緒、魚俱羅等討之，不克。

translations.literal: Sui sent the generals Tuwenshu and Yu Jurong and others to attack them, but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui court sent Generals Tuwenshu, Yu Jurong, and others against them, but they failed to win.

sentences.zh: 世充為其偏將，募江都萬餘人，頻擊破之。

translations.literal: Shichong served as a subordinate general, recruited more than ten thousand men from Jiangdu, and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong served as a subordinate commander, raised more than ten thousand men from Jiangdu, and repeatedly routed them.

sentences.zh: 每有克捷，必歸功於下，所獲軍實，皆推與士卒，由此人爭為用，功最居多。

translations.literal: Whenever there was victory he always attributed the merit to his subordinates; the military goods captured he always gave to the soldiers; for this reason men competed to serve him, and his achievements were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: After every victory he credited his subordinates and gave the captured supplies to the rank and file; men therefore rushed to follow him, and his record of achievement stood first.

sentences.zh: 十年，齊郡賊帥孟讓自長白山寇掠諸郡，至盱眙，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the bandit chief Meng Rang of Qi Commandery, coming from Mount Changbai, plundered the commanderies and reached Xuyi with more than a hundred thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the bandit leader Meng Rang of Qi Commandery swept down from Mount Changbai, raided the commanderies, and reached Xuyi at the head of more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世充以兵拒之，保都梁山，為五柵，相持不戰，乃倡言兵走，羸師示弱。

translations.literal: Shichong met him with troops, held Mount Duliang, built five palisades, faced each other without fighting, then publicly declared his army was fleeing and displayed a weakened force.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong met him with troops, held Mount Duliang behind five palisades, refused battle, then spread word that his army was retreating and deliberately showed weakness.

sentences.zh: 讓笑曰：「王世充文法小吏，安能領兵？

translations.literal: Rang laughed and said, "Wang Shichong is a petty clerk of legal texts—how can he command troops?
translations.idiomatic: Rang laughed and said, "Wang Shichong is a petty legal clerk—what does he know of command?

sentences.zh: 吾令生縛取之，鼓行而入江都。」

translations.literal: I shall have him taken alive and bound, and march straight into Jiangdu."
translations.idiomatic: I'll have him taken alive and bound, then march straight into Jiangdu."

sentences.zh: 時百姓皆入壁，野無所掠，賊眾漸餒，又苦柵當其道，不得南侵，即分兵圍五柵。

translations.literal: At that time the common people had all entered fortified settlements and there was nothing to plunder in the open country; the bandit host gradually grew hungry, and because the palisades blocked their path they could not push south; they therefore divided their forces to surround the five palisades.
translations.idiomatic: The people had all withdrawn into walled settlements, leaving nothing to raid in the countryside; the bandits grew hungry, and the palisades blocked their southward advance, so they split up and besieged the five camps.

sentences.zh: 世充每日擊之，陽不利，走還入柵。

translations.literal: Each day Shichong attacked them, feigning defeat and retreating into the palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong attacked them every day, pretended to lose, and fell back into the palisades.

sentences.zh: 如是數日，讓益輕之，乃稍分人於南方抄，留兵才足以圍柵。

translations.literal: After several days of this, Rang grew even more contemptuous and gradually sent men south to forage, leaving only enough troops to maintain the siege.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Rang grew even more contemptuous and gradually sent men south to forage, leaving only enough troops to keep up the siege.

sentences.zh: 世充知其懈，乃於營中夷灶撤幕，投方陣，四面外向，毀柵而出，奮擊，大破之，讓以數十騎遁去，斬首萬餘級，俘虜十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Shichong, knowing they had slackened, then within the camp leveled the stoves, removed the tents, formed a square battle array facing outward on all four sides, broke down the palisades and sallied forth, struck fiercely, and routed them utterly; Rang fled with several dozen horsemen; more than ten thousand heads were cut off and more than a hundred thousand captives taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong saw their guard relax, he leveled the camp stoves, stripped the tents, formed a square facing outward on all four sides, tore down the palisades, charged out, and smashed them; Rang escaped with a few dozen horsemen while more than ten thousand heads were taken and more than a hundred thousand men captured.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以世充有將帥才略，復遣領兵討諸小盜，所向盡平。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Shichong had talent and strategy as a commander, again sent him to lead troops against the lesser bandits; wherever he went he pacified them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, judging that Shichong had real command ability, again sent him against the lesser bandits and wherever he went he cleared them out.

sentences.zh: 十一年，突厥圍煬帝於雁門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Turks besieged the Emperor at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Turks besieged the Emperor at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 世充盡發江都人將往赴難，在軍中蓬首垢面，悲泣無度，曉夜不解甲，藉草而臥。

translations.literal: Shichong mobilized all the men of Jiangdu to go to the rescue; in the army he went with disheveled hair and a filthy face, wept without measure, day and night did not remove his armor, and slept on grass.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong mustered every man in Jiangdu to march to the rescue; on campaign he let his hair hang unkempt, smeared his face with dirt, wept without restraint, never doffed his armor day or night, and slept on bare grass.

sentences.zh: 煬帝聞之，以為忠，益信任之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he thought it loyalty and trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took this for loyalty and trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷江都通守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to defender of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to defender of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 時厭次人格謙為盜數年，兵十餘萬在豆子中，為太僕卿楊義臣所殺，世充帥師擊其餘眾，破之。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Qian of Yanci had been a bandit for several years with more than a hundred thousand troops in the Douzi region; the Grand Stablemaster Yang Yichen killed him; Shichong led troops to strike the remaining host and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Qian of Yanci had led bandits for years with more than a hundred thousand men in the Douzi hills until Grand Stablemaster Yang Yichen killed him; Shichong then struck the survivors and broke them.

sentences.zh: 又擊盧明月於南陽，虜獲數萬。

translations.literal: He also attacked Lu Mingyue at Nanyang and captured several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Lu Mingyue at Nanyang and took several tens of thousands captive.

sentences.zh: 後還江都，煬帝大悅，自執杯酒以賜之。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Jiangdu; the Emperor was greatly pleased and personally raised a cup of wine to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Jiangdu the Emperor was delighted and personally raised a cup of wine to honor him.

sentences.zh: 及李密攻陷洛口倉，進逼東都，煬帝特詔世充大發兵，於洛口拒密，前後百餘戰，未有勝負。

translations.literal: When Li Mi captured Luokou Granary and pressed close on the Eastern Capital, the Emperor specially ordered Shichong to raise a great army and hold Luokou against Mi; over more than a hundred battles before and after, neither side won decisively.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Mi seized Luokou Granary and pressed the Eastern Capital, the Emperor ordered Shichong to raise a great army to hold Luokou against him; they fought more than a hundred engagements without a clear victor.

sentences.zh: 又遣就軍拜世充為將軍，趣令破賊。

translations.literal: He also sent an envoy to the army to appoint Shichong general and urgently ordered him to break the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent envoys to camp to appoint Shichong general and urgently ordered him to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 世充引軍渡洛水，與李密戰，世充軍敗績，溺死者萬餘人，乃率餘眾歸河陽。

translations.literal: Shichong led his army across the Luo River to fight Li Mi; Shichong's army was utterly defeated, more than ten thousand drowned, and he then led the remnant host back to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong crossed the Luo to give battle to Li Mi and was routed; more than ten thousand drowned, and he withdrew the survivors to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 時天寒大雪，兵士在道凍死者又數萬人，比至河陽，才以千數。

translations.literal: At that time the weather was cold with heavy snow; on the road soldiers again froze to death by the tens of thousands; by the time they reached Heyang, only about a thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitter cold and snowing heavily; tens of thousands more froze to death on the march, and by the time they reached Heyang only about a thousand men remained.

sentences.zh: 世充自繫獄請罪，越王侗遣使赦之，徵還洛陽，置營於含嘉倉城，收合亡散，復得萬餘人。

translations.literal: Shichong bound himself and asked punishment; the Prince of Yue, Tong, sent envoys to pardon him, summoned him back to Luoyang, and encamped at Hanjiacang city, gathering the scattered and recovering more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong put himself in bonds to ask punishment; Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent envoys to pardon him, recalled him to Luoyang, and set camp at Hanjiacang, where he gathered the scattered and recovered more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 俄而宇文化及作難，太府卿元文都、武衛將軍皇甫無逸、右司郎中盧楚，奉越王侗嗣位於東都，拜世充為吏部尚書，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: Before long Yuwen Huaji made his coup; the Grand Treasury Director Yuan Wendu, Martial Guard General Huangfu Wuyi, and Right Department Aide Lu Chu installed the Prince of Yue Tong as successor at the Eastern Capital, appointing Shichong Minister of the Civil Service and enfeoffing him as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Huaji rebelled; Grand Treasury Director Yuan Wendu, Martial Guard General Huangfu Wuyi, and Right Department Aide Lu Chu installed Prince of Yue Yang Tong at the Eastern Capital, made Shichong Minister of the Civil Service, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 文都謂楚等曰：「今化及弒逆，讎恥未報，吾雖志在枕戈，而力所不及。

translations.literal: Wendu said to Chu and the others, "Now Huaji has committed regicide and the shame of vengeance is unavenged; though my will is to sleep on my spear, my strength does not reach that far.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu told Chu and the others, "Huaji has murdered the Emperor and our vengeance is still unpaid; though I would sleep on my spear, I lack the strength for it.

sentences.zh: 為國計者，莫如以尊官寵李密，以庫物權啖之，使擊化及，令兩賊自鬬，化及既破，而密之兵固亦疲矣。

translations.literal: For the state's interest, nothing surpasses honoring Li Mi with high office, tempting him with treasury goods, and having him attack Huaji, so that the two bandits fight each other; once Huaji is broken, Mi's army will surely also be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: For the state's sake we should honor Li Mi with high rank, tempt him with treasury goods, and set him on Huaji so the two rebels tear each other apart; once Huaji falls, Mi's army will be spent as well.

sentences.zh: 又其士卒得我之賞，居我之官，內外相親，易為反間，我師養力以乘其弊，則密亦可圖也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if his soldiers receive our rewards and hold our offices, inside and outside will be bound in kinship, and sowing discord will be easy; our army can gather strength and strike when they are spent, and then Mi too can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: And if his soldiers take our rewards and our offices, inner and outer circles will draw close and subversion will be easy; we can husband our strength and strike when they are worn down, and then Mi too can be taken."

sentences.zh: 楚等以為然。

translations.literal: Chu and the others thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 即日遣使拜密為太尉、尚書令，令討化及。

translations.literal: That very day they sent envoys to appoint Mi Grand Commandant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and ordered him to attack Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: That same day they sent envoys to appoint Mi Grand Commandant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and ordered him against Huaji.

sentences.zh: 密遂稱臣奉制，以兵拒化及於黎陽。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon declared himself subject and obeyed the imperial command, using his army to block Huaji at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi thereupon declared himself a subject, accepted the imperial orders, and met Huaji with arms at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 每戰勝，則遣使告捷，眾皆悅。

translations.literal: Whenever he won a battle he sent envoys to report victory, and all were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After each victory he sent envoys with news of success, and everyone rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 世充獨謂其麾下諸將曰：「文都之輩，刀筆吏耳，吾觀其勢，必為李密所擒。

translations.literal: Shichong alone said to the generals under him, "Men like Wendu are mere clerks with writing brushes; I see that in their situation they will surely be captured by Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong alone told his commanders, "Wendu's crowd are nothing but brush-wielding clerks; in their position they'll be taken by Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 且吾軍人每與密戰，殺其父兄子弟，前後已多，一旦為之下，吾屬無類矣！」

translations.literal: Moreover, our soldiers have fought Mi time and again and killed his fathers, elder brothers, and younger brothers and sons—already many in number; once we are placed under him, none of us will survive!"
translations.idiomatic: And our men have fought Mi again and again and killed his fathers, brothers, and sons—many of them; once we submit to him, none of us will be left alive!"

sentences.zh: 出言以激怒其眾。

translations.literal: He spoke thus to rouse his troops to anger.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke thus to inflame his troops.

sentences.zh: 文都知而大懼，與楚等謀，因世充入內，伏甲而殺之，期有日矣。

translations.literal: When Wendu learned of it he was greatly afraid; with Chu and the others he plotted that when Shichong entered the palace they would hide armed men and kill him; a date was set.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu learned of it and was terrified; with Chu and the others he plotted to hide armed men and kill Shichong when he entered the palace; a day was fixed.

sentences.zh: 納言段達庸懦，恐事不果，遣其女婿張志以楚等謀告世充。

translations.literal: The Chief Censor Duan Da was timid and feared the affair would fail; he sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to tell Shichong of Chu and the others' plot.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Censor Duan Da was timid and feared failure; he sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to warn Shichong of the plot by Chu and the others.

sentences.zh: 其夜，勒兵圍宮城，將軍費曜、田闍等拒戰於東太陽門外，曜軍敗，世充遂攻門而入，無逸以單騎遁走，獲楚殺之。

translations.literal: That night he led troops to surround the palace city; the generals Fei Yao and Tian Shan and others resisted at the outer gate of the Eastern Sun; Yao's army was defeated; Shichong then attacked the gate and entered; Wuyi fled alone on horseback; Chu was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night he led troops to surround the palace; Generals Fei Yao and Tian Shan resisted at the outer Eastern Sun Gate; Yao's force was broken; Shichong forced the gate, Wuyi fled alone on horseback, and Chu was taken and killed.

sentences.zh: 時宮門閉，世充遣人扣門言於侗曰：「元文都等欲執皇帝降於李密，段達知而告臣，臣非敢反，誅反者耳。」

translations.literal: At that time the palace gates were closed; Shichong sent men to knock and speak to Tong, saying, "Yuan Wendu and the others wished to seize the Emperor and surrender to Li Mi; Duan Da learned of it and told me; I dare not rebel—I am merely executing rebels."
translations.idiomatic: The palace gates were shut; Shichong sent men to knock and tell Tong, "Yuan Wendu and the others meant to seize Your Majesty and surrender to Li Mi; Duan Da learned of it and told me; I do not rebel—I am killing rebels."

sentences.zh: 初，文都聞變，入奉侗於乾陽殿，陳兵衛之，令將帥乘城以拒難。

translations.literal: At first, when Wendu heard of the disturbance, he entered to attend on Tong in the Qianyang Hall, arrayed troops to guard him, and ordered the commanders to mount the walls to resist the danger.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendu first heard of the uprising he brought Tong to the Qianyang Hall, posted guards, and ordered the commanders to man the walls.

sentences.zh: 段達矯侗命，執文都送於世充，至則亂擊而死。

translations.literal: Duan Da, forging Tong's command, seized Wendu and sent him to Shichong; when he arrived he was beaten to death in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da, forging Tong's order, seized Wendu and sent him to Shichong, who had him beaten to death on arrival.

sentences.zh: 達又矯侗命，開門以納世充。

translations.literal: Duan Da again forged Tong's command and opened the gate to admit Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da again forged Tong's order and opened the gate to admit Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充悉遣人代宿衛者，然後入謁陳謝曰：「文都等無狀，謀相屠害，事急為此，不敢背國。」

translations.literal: Shichong sent men to replace all the palace guards, then entered to pay respects and apologize, saying, "Wendu and the others behaved wickedly and plotted mutual slaughter; the affair was urgent and I acted thus; I dare not turn against the state."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong replaced every palace guard, then entered to apologize: "Wendu and the others plotted murder; the crisis forced my hand; I have not turned against the state."

sentences.zh: 侗與之盟。

translations.literal: Tong made a covenant with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong made a covenant with him.

sentences.zh: 其日，進拜尚書左僕射，總督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: That day he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and given overall command of all military affairs inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with overall command of all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 世充去含嘉城，移居尚書省，專宰朝政。

translations.literal: Shichong left Hanjiacang city and moved his residence to the Imperial Secretariat, monopolizing court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong quit Hanjiacang and moved into the Imperial Secretariat, seizing control of the court.

sentences.zh: 以其兄世惲為內史令，入居禁中，子弟咸擁兵馬，鎮諸城邑。

translations.literal: He made his elder brother Shiyun Chief Secretary and had him live within the forbidden precinct; his sons and younger brothers all held troops and horses and guarded the cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: He made his elder brother Shiyun Chief Secretary and lodged him in the inner palace; his sons and brothers all held troops and garrisoned the towns.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李密破化及還，其勁兵良馬多戰死，士卒疲倦。

translations.literal: Before long Li Mi defeated Huaji and returned; his crack troops and fine horses had mostly died in battle and the soldiers were weary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Mi defeated Huaji and returned, but his best troops and horses were mostly dead and his men exhausted.

sentences.zh: 世充欲乘其弊而擊之，恐人心不一，乃假托鬼神，言夢見周公。

translations.literal: Shichong wished to strike while they were spent but feared hearts were not united; he therefore falsely invoked spirits and said he had dreamed of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong wanted to strike while they were spent but feared disunity; he therefore feigned a vision and said he had dreamed of the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 乃立祠於洛水，遣巫宣言周公欲令僕射急討李密，當有大功，不則兵皆疫死。

translations.literal: He then erected a shrine at the Luo River and sent shamans to declare that the Duke of Zhou wished the Vice Director to hurry and attack Li Mi, for then there would be great merit; otherwise the soldiers would all die of plague.
translations.idiomatic: He built a shrine at the Luo and sent shamans to proclaim that the Duke of Zhou wanted the Vice Director to attack Li Mi at once for great merit—or else the army would die of plague.

sentences.zh: 世充兵多楚人，俗信妖言，眾皆請戰。

translations.literal: Shichong's troops were mostly men of Chu; the custom there believed in occult talk; all asked to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Shichong's troops were men of Chu, where omens were trusted; all clamored to fight.

sentences.zh: 世充簡練精勇，得二萬餘人，馬二千餘匹，軍於洛水南。

translations.literal: Shichong selected and drilled elite brave men, obtaining more than twenty thousand, with more than two thousand horses, and encamped south of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong drilled picked veterans—more than twenty thousand men and two thousand horses—and camped south of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 密軍偃師北山上。

translations.literal: Mi's army was on Mount Beishan at Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi's army lay on Mount Beishan at Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 時密新破化及，有輕世充之心，不設壁壘。

translations.literal: At that time Mi had newly defeated Huaji and held Shichong in contempt; he did not set up ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from defeating Huaji, Mi despised Shichong and built no fortifications.

sentences.zh: 世充夜遣三百餘騎潛入北山，伏溪谷中，令軍人秣馬蓐食，遲明而薄密。

translations.literal: Shichong by night sent more than three hundred horsemen to steal into the northern mountain, hide in ravines and valleys, ordered the soldiers to feed their horses and eat in bedrolls, and at dawn pressed close on Mi.
translations.idiomatic: By night Shichong sent more than three hundred horsemen to slip onto the northern mountain and lie in the ravines; the men fed their horses and ate from their bedrolls, then at dawn closed on Mi.

sentences.zh: 密出兵應之，陳未成列而兩軍合戰。

translations.literal: Mi sent troops to meet them; before the battle lines were formed the two armies joined in combat.
translations.idiomatic: Mi sent troops to meet them; the two armies collided before his lines were set.

sentences.zh: 其伏兵發，乘高而下，馳壓密營，又縱火焚其廬舍，密軍潰，降其將張童仁、陳智略，進下偃師，密走保洛口。

translations.literal: The ambush troops sprang up, charged down from the heights, galloped over Mi's camp, and also set fire and burned his huts; Mi's army collapsed; his generals Zhang Tongren and Chen Zhilue surrendered; he took Yanshi; Mi fled to hold Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush burst forth, charged down the heights, trampled Mi's camp, and set the huts ablaze; Mi's army broke; Generals Zhang Tongren and Chen Zhilue surrendered; Yanshi fell; Mi fled to Luokou.

sentences.zh: 初，世充兄世偉及子玄應隨化及至東郡，密得而囚之於城中，至是盡獲之。

translations.literal: At first Shichong's elder brother Shiwei and son Xuanying had followed Huaji to Dongjun; Mi captured and imprisoned them in the city; now they were all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's elder brother Shiwei and son Xuanying had followed Huaji to Dongjun; Mi had captured and imprisoned them in the city; now Shichong recovered them all.

sentences.zh: 又執密長史邴元真妻子、司馬鄭虔象之母及諸將子弟，皆撫慰之，各令潛呼其父兄。

translations.literal: He also seized the wives and children of Mi's chief clerk Xing Yuanzhen, his marshal Zheng Qianxiang's mother, and the sons and younger brothers of the various generals, and comforted them all, ordering each secretly to summon his father or elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He also took the wives and children of Mi's chief clerk Xing Yuanzhen, Marshal Zheng Qianxiang's mother, and the sons and brothers of Mi's generals, comforted them, and had each secretly call out to father or brother.

sentences.zh: 世充進兵，次洛口，邴元真、鄭虔象等舉倉城以應之。

translations.literal: Shichong advanced and halted at Luokou; Xing Yuanzhen, Zheng Qianxiang, and others raised the granary city in response.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong advanced to Luokou; Xing Yuanzhen, Zheng Qianxiang, and others opened the granary city to him.

sentences.zh: 密以數十騎走河陽，率餘眾入朝。

translations.literal: Mi fled with several dozen horsemen to Heyang and led the remnant host to submit to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fled with a few dozen horsemen to Heyang and led the survivors to surrender to the court.

sentences.zh: 世充盡收其眾，振旅而還。

translations.literal: Shichong gathered all Mi's followers and returned with his army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong gathered all of Mi's followers and marched back in good order.

sentences.zh: 侗進拜世充太尉，以尚書省為其府，備置官屬。

translations.literal: Tong promoted Shichong to Grand Commandant and made the Imperial Secretariat his headquarters, fully appointing a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Tong promoted Shichong to Grand Commandant, made the Imperial Secretariat his headquarters, and fully staffed his office.

sentences.zh: 世充立三榜於府門之外：一求文才學識堪濟世務者，一求武藝絕人摧鋒陷陣者，一求能理冤枉擁抑不申者。

translations.literal: Shichong set up three placards outside his headquarters gate: one seeking literary talent and learning able to serve the age; one seeking martial arts surpassing others and breaking enemy lines; one seeking those able to redress wrongs and grievances left unaddressed.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong posted three notices outside his gate: one for literary talent and learning fit to serve the age; one for unmatched martial prowess in the assault; one for those who could right wrongs and suppressed grievances.

sentences.zh: 於是上書陳事，日有數百，世充皆躬自省覽，慇勤慰勞。

translations.literal: Thereupon people submitted memorials on affairs by the hundreds each day; Shichong personally examined them all and earnestly comforted and encouraged them.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials poured in by the hundreds each day; Shichong read every one himself and answered with earnest encouragement.

sentences.zh: 好行小惠，下至軍營騎士，皆飾辭以誘之。

translations.literal: He liked to dispense small favors; even down to the cavalrymen in camp he used fine words to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved small favors; even common cavalrymen in camp he wooed with fine words.

sentences.zh: 當時有識者見其心口相違，頗以懷貳。

translations.literal: Men of discernment at the time, seeing his heart and mouth at odds, largely harbored divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Observant men saw the gap between his words and his heart and largely kept their loyalty divided.

sentences.zh: 世充嘗於侗前賜食，還家大嘔吐，疑遇毒所致，自是不復朝請，與侗絕矣。

translations.literal: Shichong once received food before Tong; returning home he vomited severely and suspected he had been poisoned; from then on he no longer attended court and broke with Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after eating before Tong, Shichong went home and vomited violently; he suspected poison and from then on stopped attending court and broke with Tong.

sentences.zh: 遣雲定興、段達入奏於侗，請加九錫之禮。

translations.literal: He sent Yun Dingxing and Duan Da to memorialize before Tong, asking that the Nine Bestowments be granted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yun Dingxing and Duan Da to memorialize before Tong requesting the Nine Bestowments.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，遂策授相國，總百揆，封鄭王，加九錫備物。

translations.literal: In the second year, third month, he was then invested as Chancellor, given overall charge of all affairs, enfeoffed as King of Zheng, and granted the Nine Bestowments with full regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year he was invested Chancellor with overall charge of affairs, enfeoffed King of Zheng, and granted the Nine Bestowments in full.

sentences.zh: 有道士桓法嗣者，自言解圖讖，乃上《孔子閉房記》，畫作丈夫持一竿以驅羊。

translations.literal: There was a Daoist, Huan Fasi, who claimed to understand prophetic texts; he submitted the Record of Confucius in Seclusion, depicting a man holding a pole driving sheep.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Huan Fasi, claiming to read omens, submitted the Record of Confucius in Seclusion, showing a man with a pole driving sheep.

sentences.zh: 釋云：「隋，楊姓也。

translations.literal: He explained, saying, "Sui is the Yang surname.
translations.idiomatic: He explained: "Sui is the Yang surname.

sentences.zh: 干一者，王字也。

translations.literal: Gan-one is the character wang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan-one forms the character for 'king.'

sentences.zh: 王居羊後，明相國代隋為帝也。」

translations.literal: Wang stands behind the sheep—clearly the Chancellor replaces Sui as Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Wang stands behind sheep—clearly the Chancellor will replace Sui as emperor."

sentences.zh: 又取《莊子人間世》、《德充符》二篇上之，法嗣釋曰：「上篇言『世』，下篇言『充』，此即相國名矣，明當德被人間，而應符命為天子也。」

translations.literal: He also took the Zhuangzi chapters "The Human World" and "Signs of Full Virtue" and submitted them; Fasi explained, saying, "The upper chapter speaks of 'shi,' the lower of 'chong'—this is the Chancellor's name; clearly he should virtue spread through the human world and answer the mandate as Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted the Zhuangzi chapters "The Human World" and "Signs of Full Virtue"; Fasi explained: "The upper chapter says 'shi,' the lower 'chong'—the Chancellor's name; clearly his virtue should fill the world and answer Heaven's mandate as Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 世充大悅曰：「此天命也。」

translations.literal: Shichong was greatly pleased and said, "This is Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was delighted and said, "This is Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 再拜受之，即以法嗣為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and received it, then immediately made Fasi Remonstrance Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice, accepted it, and made Fasi Remonstrance Counselor.

sentences.zh: 世充又羅取雜鳥，書帛繫其頸，自言符命而散放之。

translations.literal: Shichong also gathered miscellaneous birds, wrote on silk and tied it to their necks, claiming it was a mandate of fate, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong also caught birds, tied silk inscribed with omens to their necks, and released them as signs of mandate.

sentences.zh: 有彈射得鳥來而獻者，亦拜官爵。

translations.literal: Whoever shot down a bird and brought it in was also granted rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who shot down such a bird and presented it was also given rank.

sentences.zh: 段達、雲定興等入見於侗曰：「天命不常，鄭王功德甚盛，願陛下揖讓告禪，遵唐、虞之跡。」

translations.literal: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and others entered to see Tong and said, "Heaven's mandate is not constant; the King of Zheng's merit is very great; we wish Your Majesty would yield and announce abdication, following the traces of Tang and Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and others appeared before Tong and said, "Heaven's mandate is not fixed; the King of Zheng's merit is great; we beg Your Majesty to abdicate and follow the example of Tang and Yu."

sentences.zh: 侗怒曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，若隋德未衰，此言不可發，必天命有改，亦何論於禪讓？

translations.literal: Tong angrily said, "The realm belongs to the realm of the Founding Emperor; if Sui virtue has not yet declined, this talk must not be spoken; even if Heaven's mandate is to change, what need is there to speak of abdication?
translations.idiomatic: Tong angrily said, "The realm belongs to the Founding Emperor; if Sui virtue still holds, such words must not be spoken; and even if Heaven's mandate shifts, why speak of abdication?

sentences.zh: 公等皆是先朝舊臣，忽有斯言，朕復當何所望！」

translations.literal: You are all old ministers of the former court—suddenly to have such words, what hope have I left!"
translations.idiomatic: You are all ministers of the former reign—suddenly to speak thus, what hope have I left!"

sentences.zh: 段達等莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Duan Da and the others all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da and the others all wept.

sentences.zh: 世充又使人謂曰：「今海內未定，須得長君，待四方乂安，復子明辟。

translations.literal: Shichong also sent men to say, "Now the realm within the seas is unsettled; a mature ruler is needed; when the four quarters are pacified, the son will be restored to enlightened rule.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong also sent word: "The realm is unsettled; a mature ruler is needed; when the four quarters are pacified, the son will be restored to enlightened rule.

sentences.zh: 必若前盟，義不違負。」

translations.literal: If the former covenant is kept, righteousness will not be violated."
translations.idiomatic: If our former covenant holds, I will not break faith."

sentences.zh: 四月，假為侗詔策禪位，遣兄世惲廢侗於含涼殿，世充僭即皇帝位，建元曰開明，國號鄭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he falsely issued Tong's edict to invest him by abdication; he sent his elder brother Shiyun to depose Tong in the Hanliang Hall; Shichong presumptuously ascended the imperial throne, established the era name Kaiming, and took the state name Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he forged Tong's abdication edict; his elder brother Shiyun deposed Tong in the Hanliang Hall; Shichong seized the throne, proclaimed the era Kaiming, and named his state Zheng.

sentences.zh: 先封同姓王隆為淮陽王，整為東郡王，楷為馮翊王，素為樂安王。

translations.literal: First he enfeoffed clansmen: Wang Long as King of Huaiyang, Zheng as King of Dongjun, Kai as King of Pingyi, and Su as King of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: First he enfeoffed clansmen: Wang Long as King of Huaiyang, Zheng as King of Dongjun, Kai as King of Pingyi, and Su as King of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 次封叔瓊為陳王，兄世衡為秦王，世偉為楚王，世惲為齊王。

translations.literal: Next he enfeoffed his uncle Qiong as King of Chen, his elder brother Shiheng as King of Qin, Shiwei as King of Chu, and Shiyun as King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Next he enfeoffed his uncle Qiong as King of Chen, his elder brother Shiheng as King of Qin, Shiwei as King of Chu, and Shiyun as King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 又封瓊子辯為杞王，衡子虔壽為蔡王，偉子弘烈為魏王，行本為荊王，琬為代王；

translations.literal: He also enfeoffed Qiong's son Bian as King of Qi, Shiheng's son Qianshou as King of Cai, Shiwei's son Honglie as King of Wei, Xingben as King of Jing, and Wan as King of Dai;
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed Qiong's son Bian as King of Qi, Shiheng's son Qianshou as King of Cai, Shiwei's son Honglie as King of Wei, Xingben as King of Jing, and Wan as King of Dai;

sentences.zh: 惲子仁則為唐王，道誠為衛王，道詢為趙王，道夌為燕王；

translations.literal: Shiyun's sons Rence as King of Tang, Daocheng as King of Wei, Daoxun as King of Zhao, and Daoling as King of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Shiyun's sons Rence as King of Tang, Daocheng as King of Wei, Daoxun as King of Zhao, and Daoling as King of Yan;

sentences.zh: 兄世師子太為宋王，君度為越王。

translations.literal: his elder brother Shishi's son Tai as King of Song and Jundu as King of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: his elder brother Shishi's son Tai as King of Song and Jundu as King of Yue.

sentences.zh: 立子玄應為皇太子，封子玄恕為漢王。

translations.literal: He installed his son Xuanying as Crown Prince and enfeoffed his son Xuan'nu as King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He made his son Xuanying crown prince and enfeoffed his son Xuan'nu as King of Han.

sentences.zh: 世充每聽朝，必慇勤誨諭，言辭重復，千端萬緒，百司奉事，疲於聽受。

translations.literal: Whenever Shichong held court he earnestly admonished and instructed; his words were repetitive, with a thousand threads and ten thousand strands; the hundred offices, in carrying out affairs, were exhausted from listening.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shichong held court he lectured at length in earnest tones, repeating himself endlessly; the hundred offices grew weary just listening.

sentences.zh: 或輕騎遊歷街衢，亦不清道，百姓但避路而已，按轡徐行，謂百姓曰：「昔時天子深坐九重，在下事情，無由聞徹。

translations.literal: Sometimes he rode lightly through the streets and lanes without clearing the road; the common people merely stepped aside; holding the reins he moved slowly and said to the people, "In former times the Son of Heaven sat deep within the Nine Layers; affairs below could not be heard clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he rode lightly through the streets without clearing the way; people merely stepped aside as he held the reins and said slowly, "Formerly the Son of Heaven sat deep in the palace and could not hear what happened below.

sentences.zh: 世充非貪寶位，本欲救時，今當如一州刺史，每事親覽，當與士庶共評朝政。

translations.literal: Shichong is not greedy for the precious throne; my original intent was to save the age; now I shall be like a prefect of one province, personally examining every affair and jointly appraising court policy with scholars and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong is not greedy for the throne; I meant to save the age. Now I shall be like a provincial prefect, examine every affair myself, and judge policy with scholars and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 恐門禁有限，慮致壅塞，今止順天門外置座聽朝。」

translations.literal: I fear the gates and barriers are limited and may cause congestion; henceforth I shall hear petitions only outside the Shuntian Gate."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the gates are too narrow and will cause congestion; hereafter I shall hear petitions only outside the Shuntian Gate."

sentences.zh: 又令西朝堂受抑屈，東朝堂受直諫。

translations.literal: He also ordered the western audience hall to receive those wronged and the eastern audience hall to receive direct remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the western audience hall to receive the wronged and the eastern to receive direct remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 於是獻書上事，日有數百，條疏既煩，省覽難遍，數日後不復更出。

translations.literal: Thereupon memorials and reports came by the hundreds each day; the items were so numerous that examination could not cover them all; after several days he no longer appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials then poured in by the hundreds daily; the entries were too many to read; after a few days he stopped appearing altogether.

sentences.zh: 五月，世充禮部尚書裴仁基及其子左輔大將軍行儼、尚書左丞宇文儒童等數十人謀誅世充，復尊立侗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Shichong's Minister of Rites Pei Renji and his son, Left Assistant Grand General Xingyan, Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Yuwen Rutong, and several tens of others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Minister of Rites Pei Renji, his son Left Assistant Grand General Xingyan, Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Yuwen Rutong, and several dozen others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong.

sentences.zh: 事洩，皆見害，夷其三族。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; all were killed and their three clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked; all were killed and their clans exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 六月，世惲因勸世充害侗，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Shiyun urged Shichong to kill Tong to cut off popular hope.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Shiyun urged Shichong to kill Tong and extinguish lingering loyalty.

sentences.zh: 世充遣其侄行本鴆殺侗，謚曰恭皇帝。

translations.literal: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben to poison Tong; his posthumous title was Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben to poison Tong, who was given the posthumous title Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 其將軍羅士信率其眾千餘人來降。

translations.literal: His general Luo Shixin led more than a thousand of his followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: General Luo Shixin led more than a thousand men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十月，世充率眾東徇地，至於滑州，仍以兵臨黎陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Shichong led his host east to seize territory as far as Hua Prefecture, and again brought troops to threaten Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Shichong marched east as far as Hua Prefecture and again threatened Liyang with troops.

sentences.zh: 十一月，竇建德入世充之殷州，殺掠居人，焚燒積聚，以報黎陽之役。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Dou Jiande entered Shichong's Yin Prefecture, killed and plundered the inhabitants, burned stored goods, in reprisal for the Liyang campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Dou Jiande entered Shichong's Yin Prefecture, slaughtered and plundered the people, burned stores, and repaid the Liyang campaign in kind.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，世充殿中監豆盧達來降。

translations.literal: In the third year, second month, Shichong's Palace Supervisor Dou Ludda came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, Palace Supervisor Dou Ludda surrendered.

sentences.zh: 世充見眾心日離，乃嚴刑峻制，家一人逃者，無少長皆坐為戮，父子、兄弟、夫妻許其相告而免之。

translations.literal: Shichong saw hearts daily departing; he then imposed harsh punishments and strict rule: if one person in a household fled, all regardless of age were executed together; father, son, brother, and husband and wife were permitted to inform on one another to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing loyalty drain away daily, Shichong imposed harsh law: if one member of a household fled, every age was put to death; fathers, sons, brothers, and spouses were allowed to inform on one another to save themselves.

sentences.zh: 又令五家相保，有全家叛去而鄰人不覺者，誅及四鄰。

translations.literal: He also ordered five households to guarantee one another; if an entire household fled and neighbors did not notice, all four neighboring households were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He also made every five households mutual guarantors; if a whole household fled unnoticed, all four neighboring households were killed.

sentences.zh: 殺人相繼，其逃亡益甚。

translations.literal: Killings followed one after another, yet flight increased all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Executions followed one after another, yet flight only increased.

sentences.zh: 至於樵採之人，出入皆有限數，公私窘急，皆不聊生。

translations.literal: Even woodcutters going in and out had fixed limits on numbers; public and private alike were in dire straits and none could live.
translations.idiomatic: Even woodcutters were rationed in going out and coming in; public and private life alike were unbearable.

sentences.zh: 又以宮城為大獄，意有所忌，即收繫其人及家屬於宮中。

translations.literal: He also made the palace city a great prison; whomever he suspected he seized, together with family, and imprisoned within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the palace into a great prison; anyone he suspected, with his family, was locked inside.

sentences.zh: 又每使諸將出外，亦收其親屬質於宮內。

translations.literal: Whenever he sent generals out he also took their kin as hostages within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent generals out he also held their families hostage in the palace.

sentences.zh: 囚者相次，不減萬口，既艱食，餒死者日數十人。

translations.literal: Prisoners followed in succession, not fewer than ten thousand mouths; food was scarce and dozens starved to death each day.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners numbered no fewer than ten thousand; food ran short and dozens starved each day.

sentences.zh: 世充屯兵不散，倉粟日盡，城中人相食。

translations.literal: Shichong kept troops encamped without dispersing them; granary stores daily emptied and people in the city ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong kept his army in camp without release; granaries emptied and people in the city ate one another.

sentences.zh: 或握土置甕中，用水淘汰，沙石沉下，取其上浮泥，投以米屑，作餅餌而食之，人皆體腫而腳弱，枕倚於道路。

translations.literal: Some put earth in jars, washed it with water, let sand and stones sink, took the floating mud above, mixed in rice bran, made cakes and ate them; all were swollen in body and weak in the legs, leaning on the roads for pillows.
translations.idiomatic: Some put earth in jars, washed it, skimmed the floating mud, mixed it with rice bran, and baked cakes; bodies swelled, legs failed, and men lay along the roads.

sentences.zh: 其尚書郎盧君業、郭子高等皆死於溝壑。

translations.literal: His Secretariat Aide Lu Junye, Guo Zigao, and others all died in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat aides Lu Junye, Guo Zigao, and others died in the ditches.

sentences.zh: 七月，秦王率兵攻之，師至新安，世充鎮堡相次來降。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Prince of Qin led troops to attack; when the army reached Xin'an, Shichong's garrison forts surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Prince of Qin attacked; when his army reached Xin'an, Shichong's forts surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 八月，秦王陳兵於青城宮，世充悉兵來拒，隔澗而言曰：「隋末喪亂，天下分崩，長安、洛陽，各有分地，世充唯願自守，不敢西侵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Prince of Qin arrayed troops at Qingcheng Palace; Shichong mustered all his troops to resist; separated by a stream they spoke, saying, "At the end of Sui, chaos reigned and the realm split apart; Chang'an and Luoyang each had its portion; Shichong only wishes to hold his own and dares not invade westward.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Prince of Qin drew up at Qingcheng Palace; Shichong mustered his full force to resist; across a stream he called out, "When Sui fell the realm split; Chang'an and Luoyang each had its share; I only wish to hold my ground and dare not march west.

sentences.zh: 計熊、谷二州，相去非遠，若欲取之，豈非度內？

translations.literal: Bear and Gu Prefectures are not far apart; if you wish to take them, are they not within your measure?
translations.idiomatic: Bear and Gu Prefectures are not far off; if you wanted them, they lie within your reach.

sentences.zh: 既敦鄰好，所以不然。

translations.literal: Since we cherish neighborly friendship, I therefore do not do so.
translations.idiomatic: Out of neighborly regard I have not taken them.

sentences.zh: 王乃盛相侵軼，遠入吾地，三崤之道，千里饋糧，以此出師，未見其可。」

translations.literal: Yet Your Highness greatly encroaches and presses in deep into my territory; on the road through the Three Xiao a thousand li of grain must be supplied—by this you march to war; I do not see how it can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Highness presses deep into my land; the Three Xiao road requires grain hauled a thousand li—on such a campaign I see no success."

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「四海之內，皆承正朔，唯公執迷，獨阻聲教。

translations.literal: Taizong said to him, "Within the four seas all accept the true calendar; only you persist in error and alone block imperial teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong answered, "Within the four seas all accept the imperial calendar; only you cling to error and block the throne's teaching.

sentences.zh: 東都士庶，亟請王師，關中義勇，感恩致力。

translations.literal: The scholars and commoners of the Eastern Capital urgently summon the royal army; the righteous volunteers of Guanzhong gratefully exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Eastern Capital urgently call for the royal army; the volunteers of Guanzhong gladly give their strength.

sentences.zh: 至尊重違眾願，有斯吊伐。

translations.literal: Your Highness violates the multitude's wish and therefore faces this punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness defies the people's will and therefore faces this punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 若轉禍來降，則富貴可保；

translations.literal: If you turn misfortune into submission, wealth and honor can be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: Turn from disaster and submit, and wealth and honor may be preserved;

sentences.zh: 如欲相抗，無假多言。」

translations.literal: if you wish to resist, spare the many words."
translations.idiomatic: if you choose resistance, spare the words."

sentences.zh: 世充無以報。

translations.literal: Shichong had nothing to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had no reply.

sentences.zh: 太宗分遣諸將攻其城鎮，所至輒下。

translations.literal: Taizong separately sent the various generals to attack his walled cities and towns; wherever they arrived they fell.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent his generals against Shichong's walled towns; each fell as they arrived.

sentences.zh: 九月，王君廓攻拔世充之轘轅縣，東徇地至管城而還，於是河南州縣相次降附。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wang Junkuo captured Shichong's Huanyuan County; marching east as far as Guancheng he returned; thereupon the prefectures and counties of Henan surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Junkuo took Shichong's Huanyuan County, marched east to Guancheng, and returned; then the prefectures and counties of Henan submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 竇建德自侵殷州之後，與世充遂結深隙，信使斷絕。

translations.literal: After Dou Jiande's raid on Yin Prefecture, he and Shichong formed a deep rift and messengers ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Jiande's raid on Yin Prefecture, he and Shichong broke deeply and messengers ceased.

sentences.zh: 十一月，竇建德又遣人結好，並陳救援之意。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Dou Jiande again sent men to renew friendship and also stated his intent to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Dou Jiande again sent envoys to renew friendship and offer rescue.

sentences.zh: 世充乃遣其兄子琬及內史令長孫安世報聘，且乞師。

translations.literal: Shichong then sent his elder brother's son Wan and Chief Secretary Zhangsun Anshi to return the visit and also beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent his nephew Wan and Chief Secretary Zhangsun Anshi to return the visit and beg for troops.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，世充率兵出方諸門，與王師相抗，世充軍敗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, second month, Shichong led troops out the Fangzhu Gate to resist the royal army; Shichong's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Shichong marched out the Fangzhu Gate against the royal army and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 因乘勝追之，屯其城門。

translations.literal: They pursued while victory was hot and encamped at his city gate.
translations.idiomatic: The victors pursued hotly and camped at his city gate.

sentences.zh: 世充步卒不得入，驚散南走，追斬數千級，虜五千餘人。

translations.literal: Shichong's foot soldiers could not enter and scattered in panic southward; several thousand were pursued and cut down and more than five thousand captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's foot soldiers could not re-enter and fled south in panic; several thousand were cut down in pursuit and more than five thousand taken.

sentences.zh: 世充從此不復敢出，但嬰城自守，以待建德之援。

translations.literal: From then on Shichong no longer dared to come out but clung to the city in defense, waiting for Jiande's relief.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shichong dared not sally forth but clung to the walls, waiting for Jiande's relief.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦王擒建德並王琬、長孫安世等於武牢，回至東都城下以示之，且遣安世入城，使言敗狀。

translations.literal: In the third month the Prince of Qin captured Jiande together with Wang Wan, Zhangsun Anshi, and others at Wulao, returned to below the walls of the Eastern Capital to display them, and also sent Anshi into the city to report the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Prince of Qin captured Jiande with Wang Wan, Zhangsun Anshi, and others at Wulao, brought them beneath the Eastern Capital walls for display, and sent Anshi into the city to announce the defeat.

sentences.zh: 世充惶惑，不知所為，將潰圍而出，南走襄陽，謀於諸將，皆不答，乃率其將吏詣軍門請降。

translations.literal: Shichong was alarmed and confused, not knowing what to do; he was about to break out and flee south to Xiangyang; he consulted the generals and none answered; he then led his generals and officials to the army gate to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was panic-stricken; he planned to break out south to Xiangyang, consulted his generals, and got no answer; he then led his officers to the army gate and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 於是收其府庫，頒賜將士。

translations.literal: Thereupon they seized his treasury stores and distributed them to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The victors then seized his treasury and distributed it among the troops.

sentences.zh: 世充黃門侍郎薛德音以文檄不遜，先誅之，次收世充黨與段達、楊注、單雄信、楊公卿、郭士衡、郭什柱、董浚、張童仁、朱粲等十餘人，皆戮於洛渚之上。

translations.literal: Shichong's Palace Attendant Xue Deyin, because his written proclamation was insolent, was executed first; next they gathered Shichong's partisans Duan Da, Yang Zhu, Dan Xiongxin, Yang Gongqing, Guo Shiheng, Guo Shizhu, Dong Jun, Zhang Tongren, Zhu Can, and more than ten others, all executed on the bank of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xue Deyin was executed first for an insolent proclamation; then Shichong's partisans Duan Da, Yang Zhu, Dan Xiongxin, Yang Gongqing, Guo Shiheng, Guo Shizhu, Dong Jun, Zhang Tongren, Zhu Can, and more than ten others were all executed on the Luo bank.

sentences.zh: 秦王以世充至長安，高祖數其罪，世充對曰：「計臣之罪，誠不容誅，但陛下愛子秦王許臣不死。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin brought Shichong to Chang'an, Gaozu enumerated his crimes; Shichong answered, "Weighing my crimes, execution is indeed not excessive; but Your Majesty's beloved son the Prince of Qin promised me I would not die."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin brought Shichong to Chang'an, Gaozu counted his crimes; Shichong answered, "Judged by my crimes, death is not excessive; but Your Majesty's son the Prince of Qin promised I would not die."

sentences.zh: 高祖乃釋之。

translations.literal: Gaozu thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then spared him.

sentences.zh: 與兄苪、妻、子同徙於蜀，將行，為仇人定州刺史獨孤修德所殺。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Rui, wife, and sons he was banished to Shu; as they were about to depart he was killed by his enemy, Prefect of Dingzhou Dugu Xiude.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to Shu with his elder brother Rui, his wife, and his sons; as they set out he was killed by his enemy Dugu Xiude, prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子玄應及兄世偉等在路謀叛，伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Xuanying and elder brother Shiwei and others plotted rebellion on the road and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanying and elder brother Shiwei plotted rebellion on the road and were executed.

sentences.zh: 世充自篡位，凡三年而滅。

translations.literal: From Shichong's usurpation of the throne, in all three years and he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: From his usurpation to his fall was three years.

sentences.zh: 竇建德，貝州漳南人也。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande was a man of Zhangnan in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande came from Zhangnan in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 少時，頗以然諾為事。

translations.literal: In youth he greatly made keeping one's word his business.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he made keeping his word his chief virtue.

sentences.zh: 嘗有鄉人喪親，家貧無以葬，時建德耕於田中，聞而嘆息，遽輟耕牛，往給喪事，由是大為鄉黨所稱。

translations.literal: Once a fellow villager lost a parent; the family was poor and had nothing for burial; at the time Jiande was plowing in the field; hearing of it he sighed, immediately stopped plowing with his ox and went to supply the funeral; for this he was greatly praised in the village.
translations.idiomatic: Once a neighbor lost a parent and was too poor to bury the dead; Jiande was plowing, heard of it, sighed, stopped work, and gave his ox for the funeral—after which the village praised him greatly.

sentences.zh: 初，為里長，犯法亡去，會赦得歸。

translations.literal: At first he served as village head; he broke the law and fled, but met an amnesty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as village head, broke the law and fled, then returned when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 父卒，送葬者千餘人，凡有所贈，皆讓而不受。

translations.literal: When his father died, more than a thousand came to the funeral; whatever gifts were offered he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died more than a thousand mourners came; every gift offered he refused.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，募人討高麗，本郡選勇敢尤異者以充小帥，遂補建德為二百人長。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye, men were recruited to attack Goguryeo; the commandery selected the bravest and most exceptional to fill junior commanders, and Jiande was appointed leader of two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daye men were recruited against Goguryeo; the commandery picked its bravest for junior command and Jiande was made leader of two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 時山東大水，人多流散，同縣有孫安祖，家為水所漂，妻子餒死。

translations.literal: At that time great floods struck Shandong and many people were scattered; in the same county Sun Anzu's home was swept away by water and his wife and children starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods then ravaged Shandong and scattered the people; in his county Sun Anzu's home was swept away and his wife and children starved.

sentences.zh: 縣以安祖驍勇，亦選在行中。

translations.literal: The county, because Anzu was fierce and brave, also selected him for the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Because Anzu was fierce and brave, the county also selected him for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 安祖辭貧，白言漳南令，令怒笞之。

translations.literal: Anzu pleaded poverty and reported this to the magistrate of Zhangnan; the magistrate angrily had him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu pleaded poverty before the magistrate of Zhangnan and was flogged in anger.

sentences.zh: 安祖刺殺令，亡投建德，建德舍之。

translations.literal: Anzu stabbed and killed the magistrate, fled, and joined Jiande; Jiande gave him shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu killed the magistrate, fled, and sought Jiande, who sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，山東大飢，建德謂安祖曰：「文皇帝時，天下殷盛，發百萬之眾以伐遼東，尚為高麗所敗。

translations.literal: That year Shandong suffered great famine; Jiande said to Anzu, "In the time of Emperor Wen the realm was prosperous; they sent a million troops to attack Liaodong and were still defeated by Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shandong starved; Jiande told Anzu, "Under Emperor Wen the realm was rich; a million men were sent against Liaodong and still Goguryeo beat them.

sentences.zh: 今水潦為災，黎庶窮困，而主上不恤，親駕臨遼，加以往歲西征，瘡痍未復，百姓疲弊，累年之役，行者不歸，今重發兵，易可搖動。

translations.literal: Now floods are disaster and the people are destitute, yet the sovereign does not pity them and personally drives against Liaodong; added to last year's western campaign, wounds are not yet healed, the people are weary and exhausted, and year after year of service sends men who never return; now they send troops again—it is easy to stir unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Now flood and famine ruin the people while the sovereign ignores them and marches on Liaodong; add last year's western war, unhealed wounds, exhausted folk, and men who never return from years of service—another levy will easily stir revolt.

sentences.zh: 丈夫不死，當立大功，豈可為逃亡之虜也？

translations.literal: A man who does not die should establish great merit—how can he be a fugitive captive?
translations.idiomatic: Men who refuse to die should win great merit—how can we be fugitive captives?

sentences.zh: 我知高雞泊中廣大數百里，莞蒲阻深，可以逃難，承間而出，虜掠足以自資。

translations.literal: I know that in the Gaojipo the expanse is several hundred li, with rushes and reeds blocking deep places where one can escape hardship; seizing the interval to go out, plunder is enough to support oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I know Gaojipo: hundreds of li of reed marsh where we can hide; strike when we can and plunder enough to live.

sentences.zh: 既得聚人，且觀時變，必有大功於天下矣。」

translations.literal: Once we gather men and watch the changing times, there will surely be great merit under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Gather men, watch the times, and we may yet win great merit under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 安祖然其計。

translations.literal: Anzu approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu agreed.

sentences.zh: 建德招誘逃兵及無產業者，得數百人，令安祖率之，入泊中為群盜，安祖自稱將軍。

translations.literal: Jiande recruited and enticed deserters and those without livelihood, obtaining several hundred men; he ordered Anzu to lead them into the marsh as a band of robbers; Anzu styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande gathered deserters and destitute men—several hundred—and sent Anzu to lead them into the marsh as bandits; Anzu styled himself general.

sentences.zh: 鄃人張金稱亦結聚得百人，在河阻中。

translations.literal: Zhang Jincheng of Yu also gathered a hundred men in the river marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jincheng of Yu also gathered a hundred men in the river marshes.

sentences.zh: 蓚人高士達又起兵得千餘人，在清河界中。

translations.literal: Gao Shida of Gaoyu also raised troops and obtained more than a thousand men in the Qinghe region.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shida of Gaoyu also raised more than a thousand men in the Qinghe region.

sentences.zh: 時諸盜往來漳南者，所過皆殺掠居人，焚燒舍宅，獨不入建德之閭。

translations.literal: At that time the various bandits passing through Zhangnan all killed and plundered inhabitants and burned dwellings; only Jiande's lane they did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits passing through Zhangnan killed, plundered, and burned—only Jiande's lane they spared.

sentences.zh: 由是郡縣意建德與賊徒交結，收繫家屬，無少長皆殺之。

translations.literal: For this reason the commandery and county suspected Jiande was in league with the bandits, seized his family, and killed all regardless of age.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery therefore suspected Jiande colluded with bandits, seized his family, and killed every age.

sentences.zh: 建德聞其家被屠滅，率麾下二百人亡歸。

translations.literal: When Jiande heard his family had been slaughtered, he led his two hundred followers and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: Learning his family was slaughtered, Jiande fled home with his two hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 士達自稱東海公，以建德為司兵。

translations.literal: Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea and made Jiande army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea and made Jiande army marshal.

sentences.zh: 後安祖為張金稱所殺，其兵數千人又盡歸於建德。

translations.literal: Later Anzu was killed by Zhang Jincheng and his several thousand troops all came over to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Later Anzu was killed by Zhang Jincheng and his several thousand men passed to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 自此漸盛，兵至萬餘人，猶往來高雞泊中。

translations.literal: From then on he gradually grew strong until his troops reached more than ten thousand, still moving in and out of Gaojipo.
translations.idiomatic: From then he grew until his force passed ten thousand, still moving in and out of Gaojipo.

sentences.zh: 每傾身接物，與士卒均執勤苦，由是能致人之死力。

translations.literal: Each time he humbled himself in receiving others and shared hardship equally with the soldiers; for this he could win men's death-defying loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He always received others humbly and shared hardship with his men; thus he won death-defying loyalty.

sentences.zh: 十二年，涿郡通守郭絢率兵萬餘人來討士達。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Defender of Zhuo Commandery Guo Xuan led more than ten thousand troops to attack Shida.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Defender of Zhuo Commandery Guo Xuan led more than ten thousand men against Shida.

sentences.zh: 士達自以智略不及建德，乃進為軍司馬，咸以兵授焉。

translations.literal: Shida, feeling his strategy fell short of Jiande's, advanced him to army marshal and entrusted all troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shida, knowing himself outmatched, made Jiande army marshal and gave him all the troops.

sentences.zh: 建德既初董眾，欲立奇功以威群賊，請士達守輜重，自簡精兵七千人以拒絢，詐為與士達有隙而叛之。

translations.literal: Jiande, having first taken command of the host, wished to establish a singular achievement to awe the bandit hosts; he asked Shida to guard the baggage train while he himself selected seven thousand elite troops to resist Xuan, feigning a breach with Shida and defecting.
translations.idiomatic: New to command, Jiande wanted a striking victory to awe the bandits; he had Shida guard the baggage while he picked seven thousand elites to meet Xuan, feigning a break with Shida and defection.

sentences.zh: 士達又宣言建德背亡，而取虜獲婦人紿為建德妻子，於軍中殺之。

translations.literal: Shida also publicly declared Jiande had betrayed and fled, and took captive women and passed them off as Jiande's wife and children and killed them in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shida also proclaimed Jiande a traitor, took captive women for Jiande's wife and children, and killed them before the army.

sentences.zh: 建德偽遣人遺絢書請降，願為前驅，破士達以自效。

translations.literal: Jiande falsely sent men bearing a letter to Xuan offering surrender, wishing to serve as vanguard and break Shida to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande sent a forged letter to Xuan offering surrender as vanguard to break Shida and prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 約信之，即引兵從建德至長河界，期與為盟，共圖士達。

translations.literal: Xuan believed him and led troops following Jiande to the Changhe border, agreeing to ally and jointly plot against Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed him, followed Jiande to the Changhe border, and agreed to ally against Shida.

sentences.zh: 絢兵益懈而不備，建德襲之，大破絢軍，殺略數千人，獲馬千餘匹，絢以數十騎遁走，遣將追及於平原，斬其首以獻士達。

translations.literal: Xuan's troops grew ever more slack and unprepared; Jiande struck them and utterly routed Xuan's army, killed and plundered several thousand, captured more than a thousand horses; Xuan fled with several dozen horsemen; he sent generals to pursue and overtake him on the plain, cut off his head, and presented it to Shida.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's guard slackened; Jiande struck, routed him, killed and plundered several thousand, and took more than a thousand horses; Xuan fled with a few dozen horsemen; pursuers overtook him on the plain, took his head, and presented it to Shida.

sentences.zh: 由是建德之勢益振。

translations.literal: From this Jiande's power grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: From this Jiande's power surged.

sentences.zh: 隋遣太僕卿楊義臣率兵萬餘人討張金稱，破之於清河，所獲賊眾皆屠滅，餘散在草澤間者復相聚而投建德。

translations.literal: Sui sent Grand Stablemaster Yang Yichen to lead more than ten thousand troops against Zhang Jincheng and defeated him at Qinghe; the bandit followers captured were all slaughtered; the remainder scattered in marshes and grasslands again gathered and joined Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui court sent Grand Stablemaster Yang Yichen with more than ten thousand men against Zhang Jincheng and broke him at Qinghe; captured bandits were slaughtered; survivors in the marshes gathered again and joined Jiande.

sentences.zh: 義臣乘勝至平原，欲入高雞泊中，建德謂士達曰：「歷觀隋將，善用兵者，唯義臣耳。

translations.literal: Yichen pursued while victory was hot to Pingyuan and wished to enter Gaojipo; Jiande said to Shida, "Looking through Sui generals, only Yichen knows how to use troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen pursued to Pingyuan and meant to enter Gaojipo; Jiande told Shida, "Among Sui generals only Yichen truly knows war.

sentences.zh: 新破金稱，遠來襲我，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Fresh from breaking Jincheng, he comes from afar to strike us; his edge cannot be faced.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from beating Jincheng, he comes from afar; his edge cannot be met head-on.

sentences.zh: 請引兵避之，令其欲戰不得，空延歲月，將士疲倦，乘便襲擊，可有大功。

translations.literal: I ask to lead troops and avoid him, letting him wish to fight yet not obtain it, emptyly extending months; when officers and soldiers are weary, seize the opportunity to strike and there can be great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Let us withdraw and deny him battle, drag out the months until his men tire, then strike by opportunity for great gain.

sentences.zh: 今與爭鋒，恐公不能敵也。」

translations.literal: If we contend with his edge now, I fear you cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: If we meet his edge now, I fear you cannot stand against him."

sentences.zh: 士達不從其言，因留建德守壁，自率精兵逆擊義臣。

translations.literal: Shida did not follow his words; he left Jiande to guard the walls and himself led elite troops to meet and strike Yichen.
translations.idiomatic: Shida refused; he left Jiande to hold the camp and led elites to meet Yichen.

sentences.zh: 戰小勝，而縱酒高宴，有輕義臣之心。

translations.literal: He won a small victory and then feasted with wine in high spirits, with a mind to hold Yichen in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He won a small victory, feasted heavily, and grew contemptuous of Yichen.

sentences.zh: 建德聞之曰：「東海公未能破賊而自矜大，此禍至不久矣。

translations.literal: When Jiande heard of it he said, "The Duke of the Eastern Sea has not yet broken the enemy yet already prides himself—disaster will come before long.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande heard and said, "The Duke of the Eastern Sea has not broken the enemy yet already swells with pride—disaster will come soon.

sentences.zh: 隋兵乘勝，必長驅至此，人心驚駭，吾恐不全。」

translations.literal: The Sui army, riding victory, will surely drive straight here; hearts will be alarmed and I fear we cannot preserve ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: The Sui army will ride victory straight here; panic will break us."

sentences.zh: 遂留人守壁，自率精銳百餘據險，以防士達之敗。

translations.literal: He then left men to guard the walls and himself led more than a hundred picked troops to hold difficult ground against Shida's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He left men on the walls and took more than a hundred picked troops to hold difficult ground against Shida's defeat.

sentences.zh: 後五日，義臣果大破士達，於陣斬之，乘勢追奔，將圍建德。

translations.literal: Five days later Yichen indeed utterly routed Shida, beheaded him in battle, pursued in flight, and was about to surround Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Yichen routed Shida, killed him in battle, pursued the fugitives, and was about to surround Jiande.

sentences.zh: 守兵既少，聞士達敗，眾皆潰散。

translations.literal: The guarding troops were few; hearing Shida was defeated, the host all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The guard was small; hearing of Shida's defeat, the camp broke.

sentences.zh: 建德率百餘騎亡去，行至饒陽，觀其無守備，攻陷之，撫循士眾，人多願從，又得三千餘兵。

translations.literal: Jiande led more than a hundred horsemen and fled; reaching Raoyang he saw it undefended, attacked and took it, comforted officers and soldiers, and many wished to follow; he again obtained more than three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande fled with a hundred horsemen; at undefended Raoyang he took the city, comforted the garrison, and gained more than three thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 初，義臣既殺士達，以為建德不足憂。

translations.literal: At first, after Yichen had killed Shida, he thought Jiande was not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after killing Shida, Yichen thought Jiande negligible.

sentences.zh: 建德復還平原，收士達敗兵之死者，悉收葬焉。

translations.literal: Jiande again returned to Pingyuan and gathered the dead among Shida's defeated troops, all collected and buried.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande returned to Pingyuan, gathered Shida's dead, and buried them all.

sentences.zh: 為士達發喪，三軍皆縞素。

translations.literal: He held mourning for Shida and the whole army wore white.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned Shida and the whole army wore white.

sentences.zh: 招集亡卒，得數千人，軍復大振，始自稱將軍。

translations.literal: He gathered scattered soldiers and obtained several thousand men; the army again greatly revived and he first styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered scattered soldiers—several thousand—and revived the army; he first styled himself general.

sentences.zh: 初，群盜得隋官及山東士子皆殺之，唯建德每獲士人，必加恩遇。

translations.literal: At first, among the bandit hosts whenever they captured Sui officials and Shandong scholars they killed them; only Jiande whenever he captured a scholar always treated him with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits had killed every Sui official and Shandong scholar they caught; Jiande alone always treated captured scholars with favor.

sentences.zh: 初得饒陽縣長宋正本，引為上客，與參謀議。

translations.literal: When he first captured Raoyang County Magistrate Song Zhengben, he took him as honored guest and consulted with him on plans.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took Raoyang County Magistrate Song Zhengben, he made him honored guest and consulted him on plans.

sentences.zh: 此後隋郡長吏稍以城降之，軍容益盛，勝兵十餘萬人。

translations.literal: After this Sui commandery magistrates gradually surrendered their cities to him; military strength daily grew until his battle-ready troops exceeded a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After that Sui prefects gradually surrendered their cities; his battle-ready force passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，築壇場於河間樂壽界中，自稱長樂王，年號丁丑，署置官屬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he erected an altar in the Le Shou district of Hejian, styled himself King of Changle, took the era name Dingchou, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year he raised an altar in the Le Shou district of Hejian, styled himself King of Changle, took the era name Dingchou, and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 七月，隋遣右翊衛將軍薛世雄率兵三萬來討之，至河間城南，營於七里井。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sui sent Right Wing Guard General Xue Shixiong with thirty thousand troops against him; reaching south of Hejian city he encamped at Qili Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Sui court sent Right Wing Guard General Xue Shixiong with thirty thousand men; he camped south of Hejian at Qili Well.

sentences.zh: 建德聞世雄至，選精兵數千人伏河間南界澤中，悉拔諸城偽遁，云亡入豆子中。

translations.literal: When Jiande heard Shixiong had arrived he selected several thousand elite troops and hid them in marshes south of the Hejian border; he emptied all cities in feigned flight, saying they had fled into the Douzi region.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande picked several thousand elites and hid them in marshes south of Hejian; he emptied the cities in feigned flight, claiming flight into the Douzi hills.

sentences.zh: 世雄以為建德畏己，乃不設備。

translations.literal: Shixiong thought Jiande feared him and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong thought Jiande feared him and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 建德覘知之，自率敢死士一千人襲擊世雄。

translations.literal: Jiande learned of it and personally led a thousand dare-to-die troops to strike Shixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Learning this, Jiande led a thousand dare-to-die men against Shixiong.

sentences.zh: 會雲霧晝晦，兩軍不辨，隋軍大潰，自相踏藉，死者萬餘，世雄以數百騎而遁，餘軍悉陷。

translations.literal: Cloud and mist darkened the day; the two armies could not distinguish one another; the Sui army collapsed utterly, trampling one another; more than ten thousand died; Shixiong fled with several hundred horsemen; the remaining army was all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud and mist darkened the day until the armies could not tell friend from foe; the Sui force collapsed in mutual trampling; more than ten thousand died; Shixiong fled with a few hundred horsemen and the rest were lost.

sentences.zh: 於是建德進攻河間，頻戰不下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiande pressed the attack on Hejian but repeatedly fought without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande then pressed Hejian but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 其後城中食盡，又聞煬帝被弒，郡丞王琮率士吏發喪，建德遣使吊之，琮因使者請降，建德退舍具饌以待焉。

translations.literal: Later food in the city was exhausted and they also heard the Emperor had been assassinated; Assistant Prefect Wang Cong led officials and clerks in mourning; Jiande sent envoys to condole; Cong thereupon asked surrender through the envoy; Jiande withdrew camp and prepared a feast to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When the city starved and news came that the Emperor had been murdered, Assistant Prefect Wang Cong led mourning; Jiande sent condolences; Cong asked surrender through the envoy; Jiande withdrew and prepared a feast.

sentences.zh: 琮率官屬素服面縛詣軍門，建德親解其縛，與言隋亡之事，琮俯伏裴哀，建德亦為之泣。

translations.literal: Cong led officials in plain dress, bound, to the army gate; Jiande personally untied him and spoke with him of Sui's fall; Cong bowed prostrate in grief and Jiande wept for him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Cong came in plain dress, bound, to the camp gate; Jiande untied him himself and spoke of Sui's fall; Cong bowed in grief and Jiande wept with him.

sentences.zh: 諸賊帥或進言曰；

translations.literal: Some bandit chiefs advanced and said:
translations.idiomatic: Some bandit chiefs stepped forward and said:

sentences.zh: 「琮拒我久，殺傷甚眾，計窮方出，今請烹之。」

translations.literal: "Cong resisted us long and killed and wounded many; driven to extremity he came out—now we ask to boil him."
translations.idiomatic: "Cong resisted us long and killed many; driven to extremity he surrendered—boil him now."

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「此義士也。

translations.literal: Jiande said, "This is a man of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said, "This is a man of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 方加擢用，以勵事君者，安可殺之！

translations.literal: I am about to promote and employ him to encourage those who serve their lord—how can I kill him!
