translations.idiomatic: I shall promote him to encourage loyal service—how can I kill him!

sentences.zh: 往在泊中共為小盜，容可恣意殺人，今欲安百姓以定天下，何得害忠良乎？」

translations.literal: Formerly in the marsh we were petty robbers together and might kill at will; now I wish to settle the people and pacify the realm—how can I harm the loyal and good?"
translations.idiomatic: Once in the marsh we were petty robbers and could kill freely; now I mean to settle the people and pacify the realm—how can I harm the loyal?"

sentences.zh: 因令軍中曰：「先與王琮有隙者，今敢動搖，罪三族。」

translations.literal: He then ordered the army, saying, "Whoever formerly had enmity with Wang Cong—if he dares make trouble now, his clan to the third degree is punished."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the army: "Whoever once bore grudges against Wang Cong and now makes trouble—clan punished to the third degree."

sentences.zh: 即日授琮瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: That day he appointed Cong Prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: That day he made Cong prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 始都樂壽，號曰金城宮，自是郡縣多下之。

translations.literal: He first made Le Shou his capital, calling it Jincheng Palace; from then commanderies and counties mostly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He first made Le Shou his capital, called it Jincheng Palace; from then commanderies and counties mostly submitted.

sentences.zh: 武德元年冬至日，於金城宮設會，有五大鳥降於樂壽，群鳥數萬從之，經日而去，因改年為五鳳。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice of the first year of Wude he held a feast at Jincheng Palace; five great birds descended on Le Shou and tens of thousands of birds followed; after a day they departed; he therefore changed the era name to Wufeng.
translations.idiomatic: On the Wude winter solstice he feasted at Jincheng Palace; five great birds descended on Le Shou followed by tens of thousands; after a day they left; he changed the era name to Wufeng.

sentences.zh: 有宗城人獻玄珪一枚，景城丞孔德紹曰：「昔夏禹膺籙，天錫玄珪。

translations.literal: A man of Zongcheng presented a black jade tablet; Assistant Magistrate of Jingcheng Kong Dekao said, "In antiquity Yu of Xia received the mandate; Heaven bestowed a black jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Zongcheng presented a black jade tablet; Jingcheng Assistant Magistrate Kong Dekao said, "When Yu of Xia received the mandate Heaven gave a black jade tablet.

sentences.zh: 今瑞與禹同，宜稱夏國。」

translations.literal: Now the omen matches Yu's; you should take the state name Xia."
translations.idiomatic: Today's omen matches Yu's; you should name the state Xia."

sentences.zh: 建德從之。

translations.literal: Jiande followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande agreed.

sentences.zh: 先是，有上谷賊帥王須拔自號漫天，擁眾數萬，入掠幽州，中流矢而死。

translations.literal: Earlier, the bandit chief Wang Xuba of Shanggu styled himself Mantian, mustered several tens of thousands, entered and plundered Youzhou, and died from an arrow wound midstream.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Shanggu bandit Wang Xuba styled himself Mantian, raided Youzhou with tens of thousands, and died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 其亞將魏刀兒代領其眾，自號歷山飛，入據深澤，有徒十萬。

translations.literal: His lieutenant Wei Daor replaced him in command, styled himself Lishanfei, entered and held Shenze, and had a following of a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenant Wei Daor took command, styled himself Lishanfei, held Shenze, and mustered a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 建德與之和，刀兒因弛守備，建德襲破之，又盡並其地。

translations.literal: Jiande made peace with him; Daor therefore relaxed his guard; Jiande struck and broke him and also annexed all his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande made peace with him; Daor relaxed his guard; Jiande struck, broke him, and annexed his lands.

sentences.zh: 二年，宇文化及僭號於魏縣，建德謂其納言宋正本、內史侍郎孔德紹曰：「吾為隋之百姓數十年矣，隋為吾君二代矣。

translations.literal: In the second year, Yuwen Huaji presumptuously took the imperial title at Wei County; Jiande said to his Chief Counselor Song Zhengben and Secretariat Vice Director Kong Dekao, "I have been a common subject of Sui for several decades; Sui has been my lord for two generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yuwen Huaji seized the throne at Wei County; Jiande told Chief Counselor Song Zhengben and Secretariat Vice Director Kong Dekao, "I was Sui's subject for decades; Sui was my lord for two generations.

sentences.zh: 今化及殺之，大逆無道，此吾仇矣，請與諸公討之，何如？」

translations.literal: Now Huaji has killed him—great rebellion without principle; this is my enemy; I ask to join you gentlemen in punishing him—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji has murdered him—monstrous treason; he is my enemy; will you join me in punishing him?"

sentences.zh: 德紹曰：「今海內無主，英雄競逐，大王以布衣而起漳浦，隋郡縣官人莫不爭歸附者，以大王仗順而動，義安天下也。

translations.literal: Dekao said, "Now within the seas there is no master and heroes compete; Your Majesty rose from common cloth at Zhangpu and Sui commandery officials all contended to join you because Your Majesty moved in accord with righteousness and would pacify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Dekao said, "The realm has no master and heroes compete; you rose from common cloth at Zhangpu and Sui officials flocked to you because you moved with righteousness to pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及與國連姻，父子兄弟受恩隋代，身居不疑之地，而行弒逆之禍，篡隋自代，乃天下之賊也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji was connected by marriage to the state; father, son, brothers received Sui's grace and held positions beyond suspicion, yet he wrought regicide and usurped Sui—he is the realm's bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was tied to the dynasty by marriage; his family held unsuspected rank yet wrought regicide and usurped Sui—he is the realm's bandit.

sentences.zh: 此而不誅，安用盟主！」

translations.literal: If this is not executed, what use is an alliance leader!"
translations.idiomatic: If he is not punished, what use is a leader!"

sentences.zh: 建德稱善。

translations.literal: Jiande praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande approved.

sentences.zh: 即日引兵討化及，連戰，大破之。

translations.literal: That day he led troops to attack Huaji; in successive battles he utterly routed him.
translations.idiomatic: That day he marched on Huaji and routed him in successive battles.

sentences.zh: 化及保聊城，建德縱撞車拋石，機巧絕妙，四面攻城，陷之。

translations.literal: Huaji held Liaocheng; Jiande deployed battering rams and catapults with marvelous ingenuity, attacked on four sides, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji held Liaocheng; Jiande deployed ingenious battering engines and catapults, attacked on four sides, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 建德入城，先謁隋蕭皇后，與語稱臣。

translations.literal: Jiande entered the city and first paid respects to Empress Xiao of Sui and addressed her as subject.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the city, Jiande first paid respects to Empress Xiao of Sui and styled himself her subject.

sentences.zh: 悉收弒煬帝元謀者宇文智及、楊士覽、元武達、許弘仁、孟景，集隋文武官，對而斬之，梟首轅門之外。

translations.literal: He gathered all who had plotted the Emperor's murder—Yuwen Zhiqi, Yang Shilan, Yuan Wuda, Xu Hongren, and Meng Jing—assembled Sui civil and military officials, and beheaded them facing one another; their heads were displayed outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the regicides Yuwen Zhiqi, Yang Shilan, Yuan Wuda, Xu Hongren, and Meng Jing, assembled Sui officials, and beheaded them in pairs; their heads hung outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 化及並其二子同載以檻車，至大陸縣斬之。

translations.literal: Huaji together with his two sons was loaded in a caged cart; at Dailu County they were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji and his two sons were loaded in a cage cart and beheaded at Dailu County.

sentences.zh: 建德每平城破陣，所得資財，並散賞諸將，一無所取。

translations.literal: Whenever Jiande pacified a city or broke an enemy line, the goods obtained he distributed and rewarded to the generals, taking nothing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jiande took a city or broke a line, he distributed the spoils to his generals and kept nothing.

sentences.zh: 又不啖肉，常食唯有菜蔬、脫粟之飯。

translations.literal: He also did not eat meat; his usual food was only vegetables and husked millet rice.
translations.idiomatic: He ate no meat; his daily fare was vegetables and husked millet.

sentences.zh: 其妻曹氏不衣紈綺，所使婢妾才十數人。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Cao did not wear silk; the maids and concubines she used numbered only a dozen or so.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Cao wore no silk; her maids numbered only a dozen.

sentences.zh: 至此，得宮人以千數，並有容色，應時放散。

translations.literal: By now he had obtained palace women by the thousand, all with beauty; he released them at once.
translations.idiomatic: By now he had taken a thousand palace women of beauty; he released them at once.

sentences.zh: 得隋文武官及驍果尚且一萬，亦放散，聽其所去。

translations.literal: He obtained more than ten thousand Sui civil and military officials and brave guards still remaining and also released them, letting them go where they wished.
translations.idiomatic: He also released more than ten thousand remaining Sui officials and guards, free to go where they wished.

sentences.zh: 又以隋黃門侍郎裴矩為尚書左僕射，兵部侍郎崔君肅為侍中，少府令何稠為工部尚書，自余隨才拜授，委以政事，其有欲往關中及東都者亦恣聽之，仍給其衣糧，以兵援之，送出其境。

translations.literal: He also made Sui Palace Attendant Pei Ju Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Ministry of War Vice Director Cui Junsu Palace Attendant, and Treasury Director He Chou Minister of Works; the rest he appointed according to talent and entrusted with government; those who wished to go to Guanzhong or the Eastern Capital he also allowed freely, still giving them clothing and grain, escorting them with troops and sending them beyond his borders.
translations.idiomatic: He made Sui Palace Attendant Pei Ju Left Vice Director, Ministry of War Vice Director Cui Junsu Palace Attendant, and Treasury Director He Chou Minister of Works; others he appointed by talent; those bound for Guanzhong or the Eastern Capital he freed with clothing, grain, and armed escort to his border.

sentences.zh: 攻陷洺州，虜刺史袁子干。

translations.literal: He captured Ming Prefecture and took Prefect Yuan Zigan captive.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ming Prefecture and took Prefect Yuan Zigan.

sentences.zh: 遷都於洺州，號萬春宮。

translations.literal: He moved his capital to Ming Prefecture and named it Wanchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his capital to Ming Prefecture and named it Wanchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 遣使往灌津，祠竇青之墓，置守冢二十家。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to Guanjin to sacrifice at the tomb of Dou Qing and established twenty households to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Guanjin to sacrifice at Dou Qing's tomb and set twenty households to guard it.

sentences.zh: 又與王世充結好，遣使朝隋越王侗於洛陽。

translations.literal: He also made friendship with Wang Shichong and sent envoys to attend on Sui Prince of Yue Tong at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also befriended Wang Shichong and sent envoys to attend Prince of Yue Yang Tong at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後世充廢侗自立，乃絕之，始自尊大，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，下書言詔。

translations.literal: Later, when Shichong deposed Tong and established himself, he broke with him; he then first assumed grand airs, raised the Son of Heaven's banners, went out and in with imperial guard, and issued documents in the language of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong deposed Tong and seized the throne, Jiande broke with him, assumed imperial airs, raised royal banners, traveled with imperial guard, and issued edict-like documents.

sentences.zh: 追諡隋煬帝為閔帝，封齊王暕子政道為鄖公。

translations.literal: He posthumously titled Sui Emperor Yang as Emperor Min and enfeoffed Prince Yang's son Zhengdao as Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously titled Emperor Yang as Emperor Min and enfeoffed Prince Yang's son Zhengdao as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 然猶依倚突厥。

translations.literal: Yet he still relied on the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still leaned on the Turks.

sentences.zh: 隋義城公主先嫁突厥，及是遣使迎蕭皇后，建德勒兵千餘騎送之入蕃，又傳化及首以獻公主。

translations.literal: Sui Princess of Yicheng had earlier married into the Turks; now she sent envoys to welcome Empress Xiao; Jiande led more than a thousand horsemen to escort her into the frontier and also sent Huaji's head as tribute to the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Yicheng of Sui had married into the Turks; she now sent envoys for Empress Xiao; Jiande escorted her into the frontier with a thousand horsemen and sent Huaji's head as tribute.

sentences.zh: 既與突厥相連，兵鋒益盛。

translations.literal: Once linked with the Turks his military edge grew all the stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Linked with the Turks, his military edge grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 九月，南侵相州，河北大使淮安王神通不能拒，退奔黎陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he invaded south to Xiang Prefecture; Hebei Grand Ambassador Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong could not resist and fled in retreat to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he invaded south to Xiang Prefecture; Hebei Grand Ambassador Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong could not resist and fled to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 相州陷，殺刺史呂玟。

translations.literal: Xiang Prefecture fell and Prefect Lu Min was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Prefecture fell and Prefect Lu Min was killed.

sentences.zh: 又進攻衛州，陷黎陽，左武衛大將軍李世勣、皇妹同安長公主及神通並為所虜。

translations.literal: He again pressed the attack on We Prefecture, took Liyang, and Left Martial Guard Grand General Li Shiji, the Emperor's sister Princess Tong'an of Chang, and Shentong were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed We Prefecture, took Liyang, and captured Left Martial Guard Grand General Li Shiji, the Emperor's sister Princess Tong'an of Chang, and Shentong.

sentences.zh: 滑州刺史王軌為奴所殺，攜其首以奔建德，曰：「奴殺主為大逆，我何可納之！」

translations.literal: Prefect of Hua Wang Gui was killed by a slave; the slave brought his head and fled to Jiande, saying, "A slave who kills his master is great rebellion—how can I accept him!"
translations.idiomatic: Hua Prefect Wang Gui was killed by a slave; the slave brought his head to Jiande, who said, "A slave who kills his master commits great treason—how can I accept him!"

sentences.zh: 命立斬奴，而返軌首於滑州。

translations.literal: He ordered the slave immediately beheaded and returned Gui's head to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had the slave beheaded at once and returned Gui's head to Hua.

sentences.zh: 吏人感之，即日而降。

translations.literal: Officials and people were moved by this and submitted that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people were moved and submitted the same day.

sentences.zh: 齊、濟二州及兗州賊帥徐圓朗皆聞風而下。

translations.literal: Qi, Ji, and the bandit chief Xu Yuanlang of Yan Prefecture all submitted at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Ji, and Yan bandit chief Xu Yuanlang all submitted at the news.

sentences.zh: 建德釋李世勣，使其領兵以鎮黎州。

translations.literal: Jiande released Li Shiji and had him lead troops to guard Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande released Li Shiji and had him guard Li Prefecture with troops.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，世勣舍其父而逃歸，執法者請誅之，建德曰：「勣本唐臣，為我所虜，不忘其主，逃還本朝，此忠臣也，其父何罪！」

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Li Shiji abandoned his father and fled back; the law officers asked execution; Jiande said, "Shiji was originally Tang's minister, captured by me; he did not forget his lord and fled back to his court—this is a loyal minister; what crime has his father!"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Li Shiji abandoned his father and fled home; officers asked to kill the father; Jiande said, "Shiji was Tang's minister, my captive; he did not forget his lord and fled home—a loyal man; what crime has his father!"

sentences.zh: 竟不誅。

translations.literal: In the end he was not executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was not killed.

sentences.zh: 舍同安長公主及神通於別館，待以客禮。

translations.literal: He lodged Princess Tong'an of Chang and Shentong in separate guest houses and treated them with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged Princess Tong'an and Shentong separately and treated them as guests.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使與之連和，建德即遣公主與使俱歸。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent envoys to ally with him; Jiande immediately sent the princess back with the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent envoys to ally; Jiande sent the princess back with them.

sentences.zh: 嘗破趙州，執刺史張昂、邢州刺史陳君賓、大使張道源等，以侵軼其境，建德將戮之。

translations.literal: Once he captured Zhao Prefecture and seized Prefect Zhang Ang, Yan Prefect Chen Junbin, and Grand Ambassador Zhang Daoyuan and others; because they had encroached on his borders he was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took Zhao Prefecture and seized Prefect Zhang Ang, Yan Prefect Chen Junbin, and Grand Ambassador Zhang Daoyuan; because they had encroached on his borders he meant to execute them.

sentences.zh: 其國子祭酒凌敬進曰：「夫犬各吠非其主，今鄰人堅守，力屈就擒，此乃忠確士也。

translations.literal: His Director of the Imperial University Ling Jing advanced and said, "Each dog barks at a master not his own; now neighbors held firm, exhausted their strength, and were captured—these are steadfast men.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial University Ling Jing said, "Every dog barks at a stranger's gate; these neighbors held firm until captured—they are steadfast men.

sentences.zh: 若加酷害，何以勸大王之臣乎？」

translations.literal: If cruel harm is added, how will you encourage Your Majesty's ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: Kill them and how will you encourage your own ministers?"

sentences.zh: 建德盛怒曰：「我至城下，猶迷不降，勞我師旅，罪何可赦？」

translations.literal: Jiande was greatly angry and said, "I reached the city walls and they still would not submit, wearing out my army—how can the crime be pardoned?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiande angrily said, "They would not submit even at the walls and wore out my army—how can that be pardoned?"

sentences.zh: 敬又曰：「今大王使大將軍高士興於易水抗禦羅藝，兵才至，士興即降，大王之意復為可不？」

translations.literal: Jing again said, "Now Your Majesty sent Grand General Gao Shixing to resist Luo Yi at Yishui; the troops had just arrived when Shixing surrendered—was Your Majesty's intent not the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing said again, "You sent Grand General Gao Shixing against Luo Yi at Yishui; his troops had barely arrived when Shixing surrendered—was your intent not the same?"

sentences.zh: 建德乃悟，即命釋之。

translations.literal: Jiande then understood and immediately ordered their release.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande understood and ordered them released.

sentences.zh: 其寬厚從諫，多此類也。

translations.literal: His generosity in accepting remonstrance was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His generosity in accepting remonstrance was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 又遣士興進圍幽州，攻之不克，退軍旅籠火城，為藝所襲，士興大潰。

translations.literal: He also sent Shixing to press the siege of Youzhou; the attack did not succeed; withdrawing, the army encircled the city with cooking fires; he was struck by Yi and Shixing was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Shixing to besiege Youzhou; the attack failed; withdrawing, the army ringed the city with campfires; Yi struck and Shixing was routed.

sentences.zh: 先是，其大將王伏寶多勇略，功冠等倫，群帥嫉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, his great general Wang Fubao was very brave and resourceful; his achievement topped all ranks; the bandit chiefs envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his great general Wang Fubao, brave and resourceful, outshone all; the bandit chiefs envied him.

sentences.zh: 或言其反，建德將殺之，伏寶曰：「我無罪也，大王何聽讒言，自斬左右手乎？」

translations.literal: Some said he was rebelling; Jiande was about to kill him; Fubao said, "I am without crime; why does Your Majesty heed slander and cut off your own left and right hands?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said he rebelled; Jiande meant to kill him; Fubao said, "I am innocent; why heed slander and cut off your own hands?"

sentences.zh: 既殺之，後用兵多不利。

translations.literal: Once he was killed, afterward using troops was often unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was killed, campaigns often failed.

sentences.zh: 九月，建德自帥師圍幽州，藝出兵與戰，大破之，斬首千二百級。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jiande personally led troops to besiege Youzhou; Yi sent troops to fight and utterly routed him; more than twelve hundred heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jiande personally besieged Youzhou; Yi fought and routed him; more than twelve hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 藝兵頻勝而驕，進襲其營，建德列陣於營中，填塹而出，擊藝敗之。

translations.literal: Yi's army, repeatedly victorious, grew arrogant and pressed an attack on his camp; Jiande drew up battle lines within the camp, filled the moat, and sallied forth, striking Yi and defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's repeatedly victorious army grew arrogant and struck his camp; Jiande formed lines inside, filled the moat, sallied forth, and beat Yi.

sentences.zh: 建德薄其城，不克，遂歸洺州。

translations.literal: Jiande pressed close on the city but could not take it and therefore returned to Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande pressed the city but could not take it and returned to Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其納言宋正本好直諫，建德又聽讒言殺之。

translations.literal: His Chief Counselor Song Zhengben liked direct remonstrance; Jiande again listened to slander and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Counselor Song Zhengben liked blunt remonstrance; Jiande again listened to slander and killed him.

sentences.zh: 是後人以為誡，無復進言者，由此政教益衰。

translations.literal: After this people took it as warning and none again offered words; thereby governance and teaching daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: After that men took warning and none spoke; governance declined.

sentences.zh: 先，曹州濟陰人孟海公擁精兵三萬，據周橋城以掠河南之地。

translations.literal: Earlier, Meng Haigong of Jiyin in Caozhou mustered elite troops of thirty thousand and held Zhouqiao city to plunder the lands of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Meng Haigong of Jiyin in Caozhou held Zhouqiao with thirty thousand elite troops and raided Henan.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，建德自率兵渡河以擊之。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month Jiande personally led troops across the river to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: That eleventh month Jiande personally crossed the river to strike him.

sentences.zh: 時秦王攻王世充於洛陽，建德中書舍人劉斌說建德曰：「今唐有關內，鄭有河南，夏居河北，此鼎足相持之勢也。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin was attacking Wang Shichong at Luoyang; Jiande's Secretariat Draftsman Liu Bin urged Jiande, saying, "Now Tang holds Guanzhong, Zheng holds Henan, and Xia holds Hebei—this is the posture of three legs of a cauldron supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: While the Prince of Qin besieged Wang Shichong at Luoyang, Secretariat Draftsman Liu Bin urged Jiande: "Tang holds Guanzhong, Zheng Henan, Xia Hebei—three legs of a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 聞唐兵悉眾攻鄭，首尾二年，鄭勢日蹙而唐兵不解。

translations.literal: I hear Tang's troops are all devoted to attacking Zheng; for two years head and tail; Zheng's situation daily tightens yet Tang's army does not relax.
translations.idiomatic: Tang throws all its strength at Zheng for two years; Zheng weakens daily yet Tang does not lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 唐強鄭弱，其勢必破鄭，鄭破則夏有齒寒之憂。

translations.literal: Tang is strong and Zheng weak; the situation must break Zheng; once Zheng is broken Xia will have the worry of cold teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Tang is strong, Zheng weak; Zheng must fall; once Zheng falls Xia will feel the cold-teeth fear.

sentences.zh: 為大王計者，莫若救鄭，鄭拒其內，夏攻其外，破之必矣。

translations.literal: For Your Majesty's plan, nothing surpasses rescuing Zheng; Zheng resists within and Xia attacks without—breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue Zheng: Zheng holds within, Xia strikes without—victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 若卻唐全鄭，此常保三分之勢也。

translations.literal: If you repel Tang and preserve Zheng, you may always keep the posture of three divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Repel Tang and save Zheng and you keep the three-way balance.

sentences.zh: 若唐軍破後而鄭可圖，則因而滅之，總二國之眾，乘唐軍之敗，長驅西入，京師可得而有，此太平之基也。」

translations.literal: If after Tang's army is broken Zheng can be taken, then by that means destroy it; gather the hosts of both states, ride Tang's defeat, drive west at length, and the capital can be obtained and held—this is the foundation of great peace."
translations.idiomatic: If Tang breaks and Zheng can then be taken, destroy it; unite both hosts, ride Tang's defeat west, take the capital—that is the foundation of peace."

sentences.zh: 建德大悅曰：「此良策矣。」

translations.literal: Jiande was greatly pleased and said, "This is an excellent stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was delighted and said, "An excellent plan."

sentences.zh: 適會世充遣使乞師於建德，即遣其職方侍郎魏處繪入朝，請解世充之圍。

translations.literal: It happened that Shichong sent envoys begging troops from Jiande; he immediately sent his Protocol Director Wei Chuhui to court to ask relief for Shichong's siege.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had just begged troops; Jiande sent Protocol Director Wei Chuhui to court to ask relief for the siege.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，建德克周橋，虜海公，留其將范願守曹州，悉發海公及徐圓朗之眾來救世充。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, second month, Jiande captured Zhouqiao and took Haigong captive; he left his general Fan Yuan to guard Caozhou, mustered all of Haigong's and Xu Yuanlang's followers, and came to save Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Jiande took Zhouqiao and captured Haigong; he left General Fan Yuan at Caozhou, mustered Haigong's and Xu Yuanlang's forces, and marched to save Shichong.

sentences.zh: 軍至滑州，世充行臺僕射韓洪開城納之，遂進逼元州、梁州、管州，皆陷之，屯於滎陽。

translations.literal: The army reached Hua Prefecture; Shichong's Mobile Grand Secretariat Vice Director Han Hong opened the city to admit them; they then pressed close on Yuan, Liang, and Guan Prefectures, all of which fell; they encamped at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Hua Prefecture Shichong's Mobile Grand Secretariat Vice Director Han Hong opened the gates; they took Yuan, Liang, and Guan Prefectures and camped at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦王入武牢，進薄其營，多所傷殺，並擒其將殷秋、石瓚。

translations.literal: In the third month the Prince of Qin entered Wulao and pressed close on their camp; many were wounded and killed and Generals Yin Qiu and Shi Zan were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Prince of Qin entered Wulao, pressed their camp, killed and wounded many, and captured Generals Yin Qiu and Shi Zan.

sentences.zh: 時世充弟世辨為徐州行臺，遣其將郭士衡領兵數千人從之，合眾十餘萬，號為三十萬，軍次成皋，築宮於板渚，以示必戰。

translations.literal: At that time Shichong's younger brother Shibian was Mobile Secretariat of Xuzhou; he sent his general Guo Shiheng leading several thousand troops to follow; combined forces exceeded a hundred thousand, styled as three hundred thousand; the army halted at Chenggao and built a palace at Banzhu to show certain battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's brother Shibian, Mobile Secretariat of Xuzhou, sent General Guo Shiheng with several thousand men; combined forces passed a hundred thousand, claimed three hundred thousand, halted at Chenggao, and built a palace at Banzhu to show they would fight.

sentences.zh: 又遣間使約世充共為表裡。

translations.literal: He also sent secret envoys to arrange with Shichong for mutual inside-and-outside action.
translations.idiomatic: Secret envoys also arranged mutual action with Shichong inside and out.

sentences.zh: 經二月，迫於武牢，不得進。

translations.literal: After two months, pressed at Wulao, they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: For two months, pinned at Wulao, they could not advance.

sentences.zh: 秦王遣將軍王君廓領輕騎千餘抄其糧運，獲其大將張青特，虜獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin sent General Wang Junkuo leading more than a thousand light horsemen to raid their grain transport; he captured their great general Zhang Qingte and took very many captives and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin sent General Wang Junkuo with more than a thousand light horsemen to raid grain convoys; he captured great general Zhang Qingte and took many prisoners and goods.

sentences.zh: 建德數不利，人情危駭，將帥已下破孟海公，皆有所獲，思歸洺州。

translations.literal: Jiande was repeatedly unsuccessful; hearts were alarmed and fearful; the generals, having just broken Meng Haigong, all had gains and wished to return to Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande lost repeatedly; morale cracked; generals fresh from beating Meng Haigong had loot and wished to return to Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 凌敬進說曰：「宜悉兵濟河，攻取懷州河陽，使重將居守。

translations.literal: Ling Jing advanced and urged, saying, "You should muster all troops across the river, attack and take Huai Prefecture and Heyang, and have a heavy general hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Jing urged: "Cross the river in full force, take Huai Prefecture and Heyang, and leave a heavy garrison.

sentences.zh: 更率眾鳴鼓建旗，逾太行，入上黨，先聲後實，傳檄而定。

translations.literal: Then lead the host beating drums and raising banners over the Taihang, entering Shangdang; first sound then substance; proclaim by dispatch and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Then beat drums and raise banners over the Taihang into Shangdang; thunder first, substance after; pacify by proclamation.

sentences.zh: 漸趨壺口，稍駭蒲津，收河東之地，此策之上也。

translations.literal: Gradually press on Hukou, gradually alarm Pujin, gather the lands of Hedong—this stratagem is the highest.
translations.idiomatic: Press Hukou, threaten Pujin, gather Hedong—this is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 行此必有三利：一則入無人之境，師有萬全；

translations.literal: Doing this surely has three profits: first, entering a land without men, the army has ten thousand safeties;
translations.idiomatic: It brings three gains: first, marching into empty country, the army is safe;

sentences.zh: 二則拓土得兵；

translations.literal: second, expanding territory and obtaining troops;
translations.idiomatic: second, expanding territory and gaining troops;

sentences.zh: 三則鄭圍自解。」

translations.literal: third, Zheng's siege resolves itself."
translations.idiomatic: third, Zheng's siege lifts of itself."

sentences.zh: 建德將從之，而世充之使長孫安世陰齎金玉，啖其諸將，以亂其謀。

translations.literal: Jiande was about to follow this when Shichong's envoy Zhangsun Anshi secretly carried gold and jade and bribed his various generals to disrupt the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was about to agree when Shichong's envoy Zhangsun Anshi secretly bribed his generals with gold and jade to wreck the plan.

sentences.zh: 眾咸進諫曰：「凌敬，書生耳，豈可與言戰乎？」

translations.literal: All together remonstrated, saying, "Ling Jing is only a bookish man—how can one speak with him of war?"
translations.idiomatic: All remonstrated: "Ling Jing is only a bookish man—what does he know of war?"

sentences.zh: 建德從之，退而謝敬曰：「今眾心甚銳，此天贊我矣。

translations.literal: Jiande followed them; afterward he apologized to Jing, saying, "Now the host's heart is very sharp—this is Heaven aiding me.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande sided with them and apologized to Jing: "The army's spirit is high—Heaven aids me.

sentences.zh: 因此決戰，必將大捷。

translations.literal: By this decisive battle there will surely be great victory.
translations.idiomatic: A decisive battle will bring great victory.

sentences.zh: 已依眾議，不得從公言也。」

translations.literal: I have already followed the multitude's counsel and cannot follow your words."
translations.idiomatic: I have followed the host and cannot take your counsel."

sentences.zh: 敬固爭，建德怒，扶出焉。

translations.literal: Jing argued forcefully; Jiande was angry and had him assisted out.
translations.idiomatic: Jing argued on; Jiande angrily had him escorted out.

sentences.zh: 其妻曹氏又言於建德曰：「祭酒之言可從，大王何不納也？

translations.literal: His wife Lady Cao also spoke to Jiande, saying, "The Chief Counselor's words can be followed—why does Your Majesty not accept them?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cao also told Jiande: "The Chief Counselor's words should be heeded—why not accept them?

sentences.zh: 請自滏口之道，乘唐國之虛，連營漸進，以取山北，又因突厥西抄關中，唐必還師以自救，此則鄭圍解矣。

translations.literal: I ask to take the Fukou road, ride Tang's emptiness, advance camp by camp to take the north of the mountains, and also have the Turks raid west into Guanzhong; Tang must return troops to save itself—then Zheng's siege is resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Take the Fukou road, exploit Tang's weakness, advance camp by camp into the northern mountains, and have the Turks raid west into Guanzhong; Tang must recall its army and Zheng's siege ends.

sentences.zh: 今頓兵武牢之下，日月淹久，徒為自苦，事恐無功。」

translations.literal: Now halting troops below Wulao, days and months drag on—you merely torture yourself; I fear the affair will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Now you stall below Wulao while days pass—you only torture yourself; I fear it will fail."

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「此非女子所知也。

translations.literal: Jiande said, "This is not what women know.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said, "Women cannot know this.

sentences.zh: 且鄭國懸命朝暮，以待吾來，既許救之，豈可見難而退，示天下以不信也？」

translations.literal: Moreover Zheng's state's life hangs morning and evening, waiting for me to come; having promised rescue, how can I see difficulty and withdraw, showing the realm I am not trustworthy?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng hangs by a thread waiting for me; having promised rescue, how can I retreat at hardship and show the realm I break faith?"

sentences.zh: 於是悉眾進逼武牢，官軍按甲挫其銳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he mustered all followers and pressed close on Wulao; the imperial army held armor and blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: He then mustered all and pressed Wulao; the imperial army held its ground and blunted their edge.

sentences.zh: 及建德結陣於汜水，秦王遣騎挑之，建德進軍而戰，竇抗當之。

translations.literal: When Jiande drew up battle lines at Sishui, the Prince of Qin sent horsemen to provoke him; Jiande advanced the army to fight; Dou Kang met them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande formed lines at Sishui, the Prince of Qin sent horsemen to provoke him; Jiande advanced; Dou Kang met them.

sentences.zh: 建德少卻，秦王馳騎深入，反覆四五合，然後大破之。

translations.literal: Jiande fell back slightly; the Prince of Qin galloped deep in; back and forth four or five rounds; then he utterly routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande fell back slightly; the Prince of Qin charged deep, wheeling four or five times, then broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 建德中槍，竄於牛口渚，車騎將軍白士讓、楊武威生獲之。

translations.literal: Jiande was struck by a spear and fled to Niukou Ford; Cavalry General Bai Shirang and Martial Guard General Yang Wuwei captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande took a spear wound and fled to Niukou Ford; Cavalry General Bai Shirang and Martial Guard General Yang Wuwei took him alive.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍中有童謠曰：「豆入牛口，勢不得久。」

translations.literal: Earlier in the army there was a children's song saying, "When the bean enters the ox's mouth, the trend cannot long endure."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a children's song in the army said, "When the bean enters the ox's mouth, the trend cannot long endure."

sentences.zh: 建德行至牛口渚，甚惡之，果敗於此地。

translations.literal: When Jiande's march reached Niukou Ford he greatly hated it; indeed he was defeated at this place.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande reached Niukou Ford he hated the omen; indeed he was defeated there.

sentences.zh: 建德所領兵眾，一時奔潰，妻曹氏及其左僕射齊善行將數百騎遁於洺州。

translations.literal: The troops Jiande led at once fled in collapse; his wife Lady Cao and his Left Vice Director Qi Shanxing led several hundred horsemen and fled to Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's army collapsed at once; Lady Cao and Left Vice Director Qi Shanxing fled to Ming Prefecture with several hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 餘黨欲立建德養子為主，善行曰：「夏王平定河朔，士馬精強，一朝被擒如此，豈非天命有所歸也？

translations.literal: The remnant partisans wished to install Jiande's adopted son as leader; Shanxing said, "King Xia pacified Hebei; soldiers and horses were strong and elite; in one morning captured thus—is this not that Heaven's mandate has a destination?
translations.idiomatic: Remnants wished to make Jiande's adopted son leader; Shanxing said, "King Xia pacified Hebei with strong armies; captured in one morning—is Heaven's mandate not elsewhere?

sentences.zh: 不如委心請命，無為塗炭生人。」

translations.literal: Better to submit in sincerity and beg for orders rather than smear the living with suffering."
translations.idiomatic: Better to submit sincerely than drown the living in misery."

sentences.zh: 遂以府庫財物悉分士卒，各令散去。

translations.literal: He thereupon divided treasury goods and distributed them entirely to the soldiers, ordering each to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the treasury among the soldiers and ordered them to disperse.

sentences.zh: 善行乃與建德右僕射裴矩、行臺曹旦及建德妻率偽官屬，舉山東之地，奉傳國等八璽來降。

translations.literal: Shanxing then together with Jiande's Right Vice Director Pei Ju, Mobile Secretariat Cao Dan, and Jiande's wife led the false officials, offering the lands of Shandong and the eight imperial seals to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxing then with Right Vice Director Pei Ju, Mobile Secretariat Cao Dan, and Jiande's wife led the court, offering Shandong and the eight imperial seals in surrender.

sentences.zh: 七月，秦王俘建德至京師，斬於長安市，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Prince of Qin brought the captive Jiande to the capital; he was beheaded in Chang'an city; he was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Prince of Qin brought Jiande captive to the capital; he was beheaded in Chang'an at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 自起軍至滅，凡六歲，河北悉平。

translations.literal: From raising troops to destruction, in all six years; Hebei was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: From raising troops to destruction was six years; Hebei was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 其年，劉黑闥復盜據山東。

translations.literal: That year Liu Heita again stole and held Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Heita again seized Shandong.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世充奸人，遭逢昏主，上則諛佞詭俗以取榮名，下則強辯飾非以制群論。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Shichong was a treacherous man who met a benighted lord; above he flattered and deceived custom to win glory; below he argued forcefully and glossed over wrong to control group opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Shichong was a treacherous man who served a benighted lord; above he flattered and deceived for glory; below he argued fiercely and glossed error to control opinion.

sentences.zh: 終行篡逆，自恣陸梁，安忍殺人，矯情馭眾，凡所委任，多是叛亡，出降秦王，不致顯戮，其為幸也多矣。

translations.literal: In the end he carried out usurpation and rebellion, indulged himself in rampancy, cruelly killed without restraint, feigned feeling to control the multitude; all he entrusted were mostly deserters; surrendering to the Prince of Qin, he did not suffer conspicuous execution—his luck was great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: He usurped the throne, ran wild, killed without restraint, and feigned virtue to rule; most he trusted were deserters; surrendering to the Prince of Qin he escaped execution—his luck was great indeed.

sentences.zh: 建德義伏鄉閭，盜據河朔，撫馭士卒，招集賢良。

translations.literal: Jiande won righteousness in village lanes, seized and held Hebei, comforted and controlled soldiers, and gathered worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande won righteousness in his village, seized Hebei, comforted soldiers, and gathered worthy men.

sentences.zh: 中絕世充，終斬化及，不殺徐蓋，生還神通，沉機英斷，靡不有初。

translations.literal: He broke with Shichong midway, finally beheaded Huaji, did not kill Xu Gai, returned Shentong alive, was deep in design and bold in decision—none of this was without a good beginning.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Shichong, beheaded Huaji, spared Xu Gai, returned Shentong alive, and showed deep design and bold decision—all had good beginnings.

sentences.zh: 及宋正本、王伏寶被讒見害，凌敬、曹氏陳謀不行，遂至亡滅，鮮克有終矣。

translations.literal: When Song Zhengben and Wang Fubao were slandered and killed, and the plans of Ling Jing and Lady Cao were not followed, he reached destruction—few keep the end as well as the start.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Zhengben and Wang Fubao were slandered to death and the plans of Ling Jing and Lady Cao were ignored, he fell—few finish as well as they begin.

sentences.zh: 然天命有歸，人謀不及。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's mandate had its destination; human planning could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven's mandate had its place; human plans could not alter it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世充篡逆，建德愎諫，二凶即誅，中原弭亂。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Shichong usurped and rebelled; Jiande refused remonstrance; the two villains were executed and chaos in the central plains was stilled.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Shichong usurped; Jiande refused good counsel; both villains were executed and chaos in the central plains was stilled.
